definition_zh: 结婚；嫁；娶；为……主持婚礼；使紧密结合
definition_en: to become someone's husband or wife, to take a particular person as a spouse, to conduct a wedding ceremony for a couple, or to join two things closely together
core_image: 两个人把各自的一只手放进同一只手里，一条线从此牵住两端
scene: 秋天的礼堂门口，两家人并肩站着，等那扇木门打开。Her grandmother married a fisherman from the next village in the spring of that hard year.
sceneCN: 这里 marry 是「嫁、娶」，指与某人结成夫妻（第 1 个义项：两个人成为丈夫与妻子）；句意为那年艰难岁月的春天，她的祖母嫁给了邻村的一位渔民。图中可辨识物件：礼堂木门、并肩的两家人、等候的人群。

pos.zh: 结婚；嫁；娶；为……主持婚礼；使紧密结合

collocations.zh: 把技巧与耐心结合起来

derivatives.zh: 由古法语 mariage 而来，与 marry 同出一源，义为「婚姻；婚礼」
出自拉丁语 maritalis（婚姻的），与 marry 同源，义为「婚姻的；夫妻的」
由 marriage 加表示「可以……的」后缀 -able 构成，义为「到了可以结婚的年龄的」
由表示否定的前缀 un- 加 married 构成，义为「未婚的」

senses.title: To become husband and wife
senses.definition: to become the husband or wife of another person, or to have a wedding with someone
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人成为夫妻，或与某人举行婚礼
senses.example: They married in a small church near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一座靠海的小教堂里结了婚。
senses.why: Latin maritus named a married man and maritare named the act of taking a spouse, so the verb begins as the name of a public bond, not of a private feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maritus 指已婚的男子，动词 maritare 指娶妻或嫁人，所以这个词从一开始就是那层公开缔结的关系的名字，而不是某种私人心情。

senses.title: To take a particular person as a spouse
senses.definition: to take someone as your husband or wife, used when the partner is named as the object
senses.definitionCN: 把某个人娶为妻或嫁为夫，通常把配偶直接放在动词后面
senses.example: She married a fisherman who had never left the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 她嫁给了一个从未离开过这片海湾的渔民。
senses.why: Because the partner is the direct object, English can say who was chosen; that is why it says marry someone and not marry with someone, unlike many European languages.
senses.whyCN: 因为配偶直接做了宾语，英语就能说出被选中的人是谁；所以它说 marry someone，而不像许多欧洲语言那样加一个表示「和」的介词。

senses.title: To conduct a wedding ceremony
senses.definition: of a priest, registrar or other official, to perform the ceremony that makes two people husband and wife
senses.definitionCN: 指神职人员、登记官员或别的主持人举行仪式，使两个人成为夫妻
senses.example: The old priest had married half the couples in that valley.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老神父为山谷里半数的新人主持过婚礼。
senses.why: The same verb serves the couple and the person who declares them married, because a wedding needs an authorized voice to announce that the bond is now in force.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词既用于新人，也用于那个宣布他们成婚的人，因为婚礼需要一把被授权的嗓子说出这层关系已经生效。

senses.title: To join two things closely
senses.titleCN: 使紧密结合；使融为一体
senses.definition: to bring two things together so that they work as a single whole, said of ideas, skills or flavours
senses.definitionCN: 把两样东西凑在一起，使它们像一体那样运作，多用于想法、技艺或味道
senses.example: The chef marries smoke and citrus in a single spoonful.
senses.exampleCN: 这位厨师把烟熏味与柑橘味融进同一勺里。
senses.why: A marriage is a lasting union, so the verb stretches that image to anything deliberately put into a lasting pair, from a sauce to two crafts practised together.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻是一种长久的联合，于是这个动词把这幅画面推到任何被有意配成一对的东西上，从一味酱汁到两门一起做的手艺。

intro.en: Marry came into English from Old French in the thirteenth century, and behind it stands a Latin word for a married man; the word has always been about a bond made in public, not about romance.
intro.cn: marry 在十三世纪经古法语进入英语，背后是拉丁语里表示「已婚男子」的词；它从出现起讲的就是公开缔结的关系，而不是浪漫。

items.en: Maritus was the ordinary Latin noun for a husband and could also be an adjective for what belongs to a married man; it supplied the base of the verb.
items.cn: maritus 是拉丁语里表示丈夫的普通名词，也可作形容词指属于已婚男子的，并成为那个动词的词基。

items.en: Maritare meant to give a woman in marriage or to take a spouse, and it treated the wedding as a legal and social act rather than a mood.
items.cn: maritare 意为把女子嫁出或娶一位配偶，它把婚礼当作一件法律与社会的行为，而不是一种情绪。

items.en: Old French marier carried the same sense and supplied the form English borrowed, and its noun mariage came along with it.
items.cn: 古法语 marier 保留同样的意思，提供了英语借入的词形，名词 mariage 也随着一起传来。

items.en: Spellings such as marien and maryen settled into marry, and the verb took both the partner and the officiating priest as its object.
items.cn: marien、maryen 这类拼写后来固定为 marry，动词的宾语既可以是配偶，也可以是主持婚礼的神职人员。

items.en: Modern English keeps the wedding sense, allows both marry someone and get married, and stretches the verb to any close pairing such as flavours or skills.
items.cn: 现代英语保留婚礼义，允许 marry someone 与 get married 两种说法，并把动词延伸到任何紧密的配对，例如两种味道或两门技艺。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wedding family and the Latin words behind it; the near group gathers verbs and nouns for taking a partner or joining two things.
note.cn: 形近组收与婚礼同族的词以及它背后的拉丁词；近义组收表示结为伴侣或把两样东西合起来的动词与名词。

entries.definition: The state or ceremony of being husband and wife, from Old French mariage.
entries.definitionCN: 夫妻的状态或婚礼；出自古法语 mariage，与 marry 同族。

entries.definition: Having a husband or wife, formed from marry with -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 有丈夫或妻子的；已婚的；由 marry 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to marriage or to a husband, from Latin maritalis.
entries.definitionCN: 与婚姻或丈夫有关的；出自拉丁语 maritalis，与 marry 同源。

entries.definition: Not having a husband or wife, formed with the negative prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 没有丈夫或妻子的；未婚的；由否定前缀 un- 加 married 构成。

entries.definition: To take someone as a husband or wife, or to perform a wedding; chiefly literary and older use.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人娶为妻或嫁为夫，或主持婚礼；多用于文学与较早的用法。

entries.definition: To marry someone, or to support and adopt a belief; from Latin sponsus, a promised spouse.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人结婚；也指支持并采纳某种主张；出自拉丁语 sponsus（订婚者）。

entries.definition: Two people who are married or in a romantic relationship, or to join two things together.
entries.definitionCN: 已婚或相恋的两个人；也指把两样东西连接起来。

entries.definition: To join two people or things so that they become one.
entries.definitionCN: 把两个人或两样东西结合起来，使它们成为一体。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for a married man, and its family keeps returning to the wedding, the spouse, and the lasting pair.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「已婚男子」的名词上，它的同族词反复回到婚礼、配偶与长久的一对。

normal.en: Latin maritus means a husband, so marry starts as a word about a public bond rather than a private feeling.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 maritus 意为丈夫，所以 marry 起点是一层公开的关系，而不是私人的心情。

normal.en: The verb maritare meant to give a bride or take a spouse, and English borrowed its French descendant marier.
normal.cn: 动词 maritare 意为把新娘嫁出或娶一位配偶，英语借入的是它的法语后代 marier。

normal.en: Because the partner is the direct object, English says marry someone; adding with would make it sound like a ceremony you both merely attend.
normal.cn: 因为配偶是直接宾语，英语说 marry someone；如果加一个表示「和」的介词，听起来就像一场你们只是出席的仪式。

normal.en: The priest who marries a couple uses the same word from the opposite side: he is the one who makes the bond official.
normal.cn: 为一对新人主持婚礼的神父从相反的一侧用同一个词：他是让这层关系正式生效的人。

normal.en: Marriage, marital and married all go back to the same Latin base, one as the noun, one as an adjective of the husband, one as a state.
normal.cn: marriage、marital 与 married 都回到同一个拉丁词基，一个作名词，一个作丈夫的形容词，一个表示所处的状态。

abstract.en: Two hands closing on each other, and the word names the closing, not the warmth that led to it.
abstract.cn: 两只手彼此握住，而这个词命名的是握住本身，不是通向它的那点温热。

abstract.en: A wedding is a sentence said aloud in front of witnesses, and marry is that sentence turned into a verb.
abstract.cn: 婚礼是一句在证人面前说出口的话，而 marry 就是那句话变成的动词。

abstract.en: Once a bond can be made official, it can be made between flavours or skills, and the old public vow quietly becomes a cook's trick.
abstract.cn: 一旦一种结合可以被正式认定，它也能在味道或技艺之间成立，旧日的公开誓言便悄悄变成了厨子的手法。

examples.cn: 他们在一座靠海的小教堂里结了婚。

examples.en: The old priest had married half the couples in that valley.
examples.cn: 那位老神父为山谷里半数的新人主持过婚礼。

examples.en: The chef marries smoke and citrus in a single spoonful.
examples.cn: 这位厨师把烟熏味与柑橘味融进同一勺里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「玛丽」——婚礼上新娘被叫作玛丽，两个人从此被叫成一家人；记住 marry 是结婚，也是嫁娶。

root: 拉丁语 maritus（丈夫、已婚的）与动词 maritare 是可靠来源，经古法语 marier 进入英语；maritus 更深一层的词源一般认为与表示「年轻男子、男性」的古老词根有关，但具体来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bond publicly made; the senses then divide into the wedding itself, the named partner, the official who declares it, and any close pairing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一层公开缔结的关系；义项由此分成婚礼本身、被点明的配偶、宣布礼成的主持人，以及任何紧密的配对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands laid into one hand, so that a single line holds both ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人把各自的一只手放进同一只手里，一条线从此牵住两端。

branches.cn: 小石教堂里交换的两枚戒指

branches.en: a bride naming the fisherman she chose
branches.cn: 新娘说出自己选中的那位渔民

branches.en: an old priest raising his hand over the couple
branches.cn: 老神父在新人上方举起的手

branches.cn: 乡村婚礼上并肩站着的两家人

intro.en: A Latin noun for a husband, its verb, one French borrowing and three English endings carry marry from a wedding contract to a cook's pairing.
intro.cn: 一个表示丈夫的拉丁名词、它的动词、一次法语借入，再加三个英语词尾，把 marry 从一纸婚约带到厨子的配对。

latinIntro.en: Latin maritus and maritare are recorded and reliable, and Old French marier is the accepted bridge into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 maritus 与 maritare 有记录且可靠，古法语 marier 是被认可的进入英语的桥梁。

definition_zh: 主人；硕士；大师；能手；精通；掌握；控制；制服
definition_en: a person who owns or has authority over something, an advanced university degree, an expert in a craft, or to learn and gain complete control of something
core_image: 老人一抬手，院子里的人和马都停下来等他的吩咐
scene: 旧宅的院子里，一位老人牵马走到廊下，抬手示意年轻仆人不必再跟着。The old master of the house knew every corner of the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 master 是「主人」（第 1 个义项：对一处宅院、牲畜或仆役拥有支配权的人）；句意为这座宅子的老主人熟悉园子的每一个角落。图中可辨识物件：廊下的马、抬手示意的老人、退后的仆人。

derivatives.zh: 由 master 加表示「状态、性质」的后缀 -y 构成，义为「精通；掌控」
由 master 加表示「充满……」的后缀 -ful 构成，义为「有掌控力的；技艺高超的」
由 master 与 piece 复合而成，本指学徒期满后用以证明手艺的作品，义为「杰作」
由 master 加 -ly 构成，义为「精巧的；显出大师手笔的」

senses.title: The owner or head of a household
senses.definition: a person who owns a house, an animal or a servant and has authority over them
senses.definitionCN: 对一处宅院、一头牲畜或一名仆役拥有所有权并有权支配的人
senses.example: The dog follows its master everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 这条狗到处跟着它的主人。
senses.why: Latin magister named the man who stood above others, and the first English uses kept that household power: the master is the one whose word is obeyed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 magister 指站在他人之上的人，英语最早的用法保留的正是这种宅院里的权力：主人就是话被听从的那一位。

senses.title: A holder of a master's degree
senses.definition: an advanced university degree below a doctorate, or the person who holds it
senses.definitionCN: 低于博士学位的大学高级学位，也指持有这一学位的人
senses.example: She took a master's degree in urban planning.
senses.exampleCN: 她取得了城市规划专业的硕士学位。
senses.why: In the medieval university the magister was the licensed teacher, so the title of the qualified teacher became the name of the highest taught degree.
senses.whyCN: 在中世纪的大学里，magister 是取得授课资格的老师，于是「合格教师」这个头衔后来成了最高的授课型学位之名。

senses.title: An expert in a craft or art
senses.definition: a person who is highly skilled in a craft, an art or a technique
senses.definitionCN: 在某门手艺、艺术或技艺上极为精湛的人
senses.example: The glass master shaped the bowl with three quick turns.
senses.exampleCN: 那位玻璃大师转了三下就把碗形定了下来。
senses.why: Because magister marked the person who had finished the whole training, skill itself came to be measured by the word: a master is the one at the top of the craft.
senses.whyCN: 因为 magister 标出的是完成了全部训练的人，技艺高低便用这个词来衡量：大师就是一门手艺里站在顶端的那一个。

senses.title: To learn or understand something completely
senses.definition: to learn a skill or subject so well that you can use it without effort
senses.definitionCN: 把一项技能或一门学问学到运用自如的程度
senses.example: He mastered the old engine by taking it apart twice.
senses.exampleCN: 他把那台旧发动机拆了两遍，就把它摸透了。
senses.why: The noun for a qualified teacher turned into a verb: to master a thing is to reach the level at which you could explain it to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 指「合格老师」的名词转成了动词：master 一样东西，就是达到能够把它讲给别人听的水平。

senses.title: To bring something under control
senses.definition: to gain control over a strong feeling, an animal or a difficult situation
senses.definitionCN: 把强烈的情绪、一头动物或困难的局面压住并置于掌控之下
senses.example: She mastered her anger before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她先把怒气压住，才开口回答。
senses.why: If a master is the person who gives orders, the verb can also mean making a wild thing obey, and the object shifts from a skill to whatever refuses to be controlled.
senses.whyCN: 既然 master 是发号施令的人，动词也就表示让不听话的东西服从，宾语于是从一门技能转到任何不肯受控的对象。

intro.en: Master comes from Latin magister, the man with authority, and reached English through Old French; the word still carries both the power to command and the title of a qualified teacher.
intro.cn: master 出自拉丁语 magister（有权威的人），经古法语进入英语；这个词至今同时带着发号施令的权力与「合格教师」的头衔。

items.en: Magis is the Latin adverb for more or rather, and it marks the greater side of any comparison.
items.cn: magis 是拉丁语副词，意为「更多、更」，标出任何比较中更强的那一边。

items.en: Magister was built on magis with a comparative ending and named the man placed above others, above all the teacher in charge of pupils.
items.cn: magister 由 magis 加比较级词尾构成，指被置于他人之上的人，首先指管教学生的老师。

items.en: Old French kept the word as maistre, a lord, teacher or craftsman, and its spelling travelled into English with the Norman court.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词保留为 maistre，指领主、教师或匠人，它的拼写随诺曼宫廷传入英语。

items.en: Middle English master covered the head of a house, the qualified teacher and the skilled craftsman, and the universities gave it to a degree.
items.cn: 中古英语的 master 兼指一家之主、合格教师与熟练匠人，大学又把这个称号给了一个学位。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb to master, keeps the academic degree, and still uses the noun for an animal's owner and for a supreme practitioner.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了动词 master，保留了学位义，也仍用这个名词指动物的主人与某一行的顶尖高手。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and Latin relatives of the word; the near group gathers names for owners, experts and the highly skilled.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的派生词与拉丁同族词；近义组收表示主人、专家与高超技艺者的词。

entries.definition: Complete control of a skill or subject.
entries.definitionCN: 对技能或学问的完全掌握；由 master 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: Showing great skill or firm control.
entries.definitionCN: 显出高超技艺或强力掌控的；由 master 加 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: Showing the authority of a master, or relating to a magistrate.
entries.definitionCN: 带有权威气派的；也与地方法官有关；出自拉丁语 magister。

entries.definition: A public official who judges minor cases.
entries.definitionCN: 审理轻微案件的公职人员；词根同为拉丁语 magister。

entries.definition: A person with special knowledge or skill in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 在某一领域有专门知识或技能的人。

entries.definition: The person who legally possesses something.
entries.definitionCN: 合法拥有某物的人。

entries.definition: Very skilled at something.
entries.definitionCN: 在某事上很在行、很熟练的。

entries.definition: A performer with outstanding technical skill.
entries.definitionCN: 技艺出众的演奏者或表演者。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin adverb of comparison, and its family keeps returning to standing above others: as owner, as teacher, as expert, as full control.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语的一个比较副词上，它的同族词反复回到「站在他人之上」：作为主人、老师、能手，直到完全的掌控。

normal.en: Latin magis means more, and magister is the person who is more than the others, so the title began as a comparison.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 magis 意为「更多」，magister 就是「比别人更多」的那个人，所以这个头衔起初是一次比较。

normal.en: Old French maistre kept the meaning and lost some letters on the way to English master.
normal.cn: 古法语 maistre 保留了意思，在进入英语 master 的过程中丢掉了一些字母。

normal.en: Master's degree goes back to the medieval university, where a magister was a teacher licensed to lecture.
normal.cn: 硕士学位可以追到中世纪大学，那时 magister 是获准开讲的教师。

normal.en: Mastery adds -y for the state, masterful adds -ful for the quality, and both keep the sense of standing at the top.
normal.cn: mastery 加 -y 指状态，masterful 加 -ful 指性质，两者都保留着「站在顶端」的意思。

normal.en: Master a skill literally repeats the old teacher image: you learn a thing until you could teach it yourself.
normal.cn: master a skill 字面上重复了旧的教师形象：你学一样东西，直到能够自己去教它。

abstract.en: Authority is pictured as a raised hand: a house, a horse and a servant all wait for the same signal.
abstract.cn: 权威被想象成抬起的一只手：房子、马与仆人都等同一个示意。

abstract.en: A degree, a craft and a command share one word because all three are proofs that the training is finished.
abstract.cn: 学位、手艺与掌控共用一个词，因为三者都是「训练已经完成」的凭证。

abstract.en: The word began as a comparison and ended as a certificate, yet both still ask who stands higher.
abstract.cn: 这个词起于一次比较，落成一纸证书，可两者都仍在问：谁站得更高。

examples.en: The old master of the house knew every corner of the garden.
examples.cn: 这座宅子的老主人熟悉园子的每一个角落。

examples.en: He mastered the old engine by taking it apart twice.
examples.cn: 他把那台旧发动机拆了两遍，就把它摸透了。

examples.en: She took a master's degree in urban planning.
examples.cn: 她取得了城市规划专业的硕士学位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马斯特」——马背上坐得最稳的那个人被喊作斯特；记住 master 是主人，也是把本事练到顶的人。

root: 拉丁语 magis（更多、更）加比较级词尾构成 magister（更有权威的人、教师），经古法语 maistre 进入英语；同族词多与权威、教导和技艺高超有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person placed above others; the senses divide into the head of a household, the qualified teacher and the degree, the top craftsman, and the verb of reaching full command.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是站在他人之上的人；义项由此分成一家之主、合格教师与学位、顶尖匠人，以及达到完全掌控的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old man raises one hand and the yard, the horse and the servants all wait for his word.
core.cn: 核心意象：老人一抬手，院子里的人、马和仆人都停下来等他的吩咐。

branches.en: a lamp lit at the door of a house whose owner has returned
branches.cn: 主人归来时宅门前点起的灯

branches.en: a hood and gown on a graduation morning
branches.cn: 毕业清晨的方帽与长袍

branches.en: a glassblower's hands turning a bowl in three moves
branches.cn: 吹玻璃的人三下转出一只碗

branches.en: an engine taken apart and put back together
branches.cn: 拆开又装回的发动机

branches.en: a raised voice stopped before it leaves the mouth
branches.cn: 抬高的话音在出口之前被按住

intro.en: A Latin comparative adverb, its comparative noun, the French form of that noun and four English endings carry the word from a lord's hall to a workshop bench.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语比较副词、由它构成的比较级名词、这个名词的法语形式，再加四个英语词尾，把这个词从领主的厅堂带到工匠的台前。

latinIntro.en: Latin magis, more, and magister, the man who is more than others, are the reliable source of the family; Old French maistre is the form that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 magis（更多）和 magister（比别人更多的那个人）是这个词族可靠的源头；英语借入的是古法语形式 maistre。

definition_zh: 比赛；火柴；相配的人或物；相配；匹配；比得上
definition_en: a contest between two sides, a small stick that makes fire when struck, a person or thing that fits another, or to fit with and be equal to something
core_image: 细木划过盒面迸出火星，两队人也正好站到对面
scene: 体育馆的看台上坐满了人，双方球员在场地两端排开，裁判把哨子放到嘴边。The final match began under a grey sky, with the crowd already on its feet.
sceneCN: 这里 match 是「比赛」（第 1 个义项：两队或两人按规则分胜负的较量）；句意为决赛在灰蒙蒙的天空下开始，看台上的人已经站了起来。图中可辨识物件：满座的看台、两端排开的球员、裁判的哨子。

pos.zh: 比赛；火柴；相配的人或物

derivatives.zh: 由 match 与 box 复合而成，义为「火柴盒」
由表示「错误」的前缀 mis- 加 match 构成，义为「不匹配；错配」
由 match 与 maker 复合而成，义为「媒人；撮合者」
由表示「不」的前缀 un- 加 matched 构成，义为「无可匹敌的」

senses.title: A contest between two sides
senses.definition: a contest in which two people or teams compete under rules to win
senses.definitionCN: 两人或两队为争胜而按规则进行的较量
senses.example: The final match began under a grey sky.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛在灰蒙蒙的天空下开始了。
senses.why: The pairing sense is older than the contest: a match was first a pair set against each other, and only later the event they played.
senses.whyCN: 配对义比比赛义更早：match 起初是被摆到彼此对面的一对，后来才指这一对人所进行的赛事。

senses.title: A small stick that makes fire
senses.definition: a small piece of wood or paper with a treated head that makes fire when struck
senses.definitionCN: 带药头的小木梗或纸梗，摩擦时起火
senses.example: He struck a match and the lamp caught at once.
senses.exampleCN: 他划着一根火柴，灯立刻亮了。
senses.why: The fire sense comes from a different word altogether, one that named the wick of a lamp before it named a stick you strike.
senses.whyCN: 「火柴」这个义项来自另一个完全不同的词：它先指灯芯，后来才指手里用来划的那种小梗。

senses.title: A person or thing that fits another
senses.definition: a person or thing that is exactly suitable for another and forms a good pair with it
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人或物恰好合适、能配成一对的人或物
senses.example: The two of them are a good match in temperament.
senses.exampleCN: 他们两人在性情上是很好的一对。
senses.why: Old English gemæcca meant a mate or an equal, so suitability was built into the word before it ever meant a game.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gemæcca 本就指配偶或地位相当的人，所以「合适」这层意思在它指比赛之前就已经长在词里了。

senses.title: To fit together with something else
senses.definition: to be the same as, or to fit together with, something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相同，或彼此契合、对得上
senses.example: The curtains match the colour of the old walls.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘的颜色和老墙很相配。
senses.why: If two things form a match, the verb names the act of bringing them into that pair, which is why colours, names and records can all be matched.
senses.whyCN: 若两样东西构成一对，动词便表示把它们配成那一对的动作，所以颜色、名字与记录都能 match。

senses.title: To be equal in strength or quality
senses.definition: to be equal in strength, speed or quality to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 在力量、速度或水准上与某人某物相当，不落下风
senses.example: No one in the class could match her speed at the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 班上没有人在实验台前比得上她的速度。
senses.why: A match is also an equal opponent, so the verb means placing yourself beside that equal and finding nothing missing.
senses.whyCN: match 也指势均力敌的对手，所以动词表示把自己摆到那个对手旁边，发现并不缺什么。

intro.en: Match is two words that came to look alike: one Germanic word for a pair or an equal, and one Latin word for a lamp wick that became the fire stick.
intro.cn: match 是两个后来长得一模一样的词：一个日耳曼词表示「一对、地位相当」，一个拉丁词表示「灯芯」，后者变成了火柴。

items.en: Gemæcca meant a mate, a companion or an equal, and it named the second half of a pair rather than a game.
items.cn: gemæcca 指配偶、同伴或地位相当的人，命名的是成对中的另一半，而不是一场比赛。

items.en: Myxa meant the wick of a lamp; it passed through Greek into Latin before it named anything that could be struck.
items.cn: myxa 指灯芯；它经希腊语进入拉丁语，那时还不指任何能划着的东西。

items.en: Old French meiche named a wick, and English borrowed it for the cord that carried fire to gunpowder and then for the little stick.
items.cn: 古法语 meiche 指灯芯，英语借它来指把火引到火药的引线，后来又指那根小木梗。

items.en: Middle English used matchen for pairing and meiche for the wick, and the two forms slowly merged in sound and spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语用 matchen 表示配对，用 meiche 表示灯芯，两种形式在读音与拼写上慢慢合流。

items.en: Modern English keeps both lines, so one word now covers a game, a small fire, a fitting partner and the act of equalling another.
items.cn: 现代英语把两条线索都留着，于是一个词同时覆盖比赛、小火、相配的伴侣，以及与他人相等这一动作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives built on match plus one close spelling; the near group gathers words for contests, fitting partners and equals.
note.cn: 形近组收由 match 构成的复合词与派生词，外加一个拼写相近的词；近义组收表示比赛、合适的伴侣与地位相当者的词。

entries.definition: A small box for holding matches.
entries.definitionCN: 装火柴的小盒子；由 match 与 box 复合而成。

entries.definition: A pairing that does not fit well.
entries.definitionCN: 配得不好的组合；由表示「错误」的前缀 mis- 加 match 构成。

entries.definition: A person who arranges marriages or brings people together.
entries.definitionCN: 安排婚事或撮合别人的人；由 match 与 maker 复合而成。

entries.definition: To walk with regular steps, or the third month; the spelling is close but the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 齐步走；也指三月；只是拼写相近，词源不同，与 match 无关。

entries.definition: A competition in which people try to win.
entries.definitionCN: 人们争胜的比赛。

entries.definition: A single occasion of play under rules.
entries.definitionCN: 按规则进行的一场游戏或比赛。

entries.definition: A person or thing that corresponds to another.
entries.definitionCN: 与另一方相对应的人或物。

entries.definition: A person of the same ability or rank as another.
entries.definitionCN: 能力或地位与他人相当的人。

normalIntro.en: Two histories meet in one spelling: a Germanic word for a pair and a Latin word for a wick, and the family keeps returning to pairing, fire and equal standing.
normalIntro.cn: 两条历史在同一个拼写里相遇：一个日耳曼词表示一对，一个拉丁词表示灯芯；同族词反复回到配对、火与势均力敌。

normal.en: Old English gemæcca meant a mate or an equal, which is why match still names one half of a good pair.
normal.cn: 古英语 gemæcca 指配偶或地位相当的人，所以 match 至今指一对中的另一半。

normal.en: Latin myxa meant a lamp wick, and that wick sense came through Old French meiche into the English fire stick.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 myxa 指灯芯，这层意思经古法语 meiche 进入了英语的火柴义。

normal.en: Matchbox and matchmaker are compounds, and both keep the pairing or the fire in plain view.
normal.cn: matchbox 与 matchmaker 都是复合词，一个把火摆在明处，一个把配对摆在明处。

normal.en: Mismatch adds mis- for a bad pairing, while unmatched adds un- for having no equal.
normal.cn: mismatch 加 mis- 指配得不好，unmatched 加 un- 指没有对手。

normal.en: Match as a verb asks you to put two things side by side until they fit; nothing is compared in the abstract.
normal.cn: 作动词的 match 要求你把两样东西摆在一起，直到它们对得上；比较从不发生在空处。

abstract.en: Pairing and fire meet in one word because both happen in a single instant of contact.
abstract.cn: 配对与火在一个词里相遇，因为两者都发生在接触的一瞬。

abstract.en: A match is a test of fit: the right two things leave nothing to correct.
abstract.cn: match 是一场契合的检验：对的那两样东西，不留需要修改的地方。

abstract.en: From a lamp wick to a whistle, the word keeps finding two sides and making them face each other.
abstract.cn: 从灯芯到哨声，这个词一直在寻找两边，让它们面对面。

examples.en: The two teams will play a match on Saturday.
examples.cn: 两队将在星期六进行一场比赛。

examples.en: She struck a match to light the candle.
examples.cn: 她划着一根火柴点蜡烛。

examples.en: No one can match his speed on the track.
examples.cn: 跑道上没有人比得上他的速度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马吃」——马要吃草，先得有人擦着一根小木梗点火；记住 match 是火柴，也是比赛和相配。

root: 这个词有两条来源：表示「一对、配偶」的义项出自古英语 gemæcca（配偶、地位相当的人）；表示「火柴」的义项出自拉丁语 myxa（灯芯），经希腊语与古法语 meiche 进入英语，两条词形后来合流。

sensesIntro.en: The core is two things brought face to face; the senses divide into the contest of two sides, the strike of a wick, the fitting partner, the act of fitting, and the equal who cannot be beaten.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两样东西被摆到彼此对面；义项由此分成两方的比赛、灯芯的一划、合适的伴侣、使彼此契合的动作，以及无人能敌的对手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin stick scrapes across a box and a spark jumps, while two teams stand face to face.
core.cn: 核心意象：细木划过盒面迸出火星，两队人也正好站到对面。

branches.en: a whistle at the centre of a packed stand
branches.cn: 满座看台中央的一声哨响

branches.en: a spark taken from a box in a dark room
branches.cn: 暗屋里从盒面擦出的一点火星

branches.en: two people pushed together and finding they fit
branches.cn: 两个人被推到一处，发现彼此合适

branches.en: curtains chosen to sit beside an old wall
branches.cn: 照着老墙颜色挑出的窗帘

branches.en: a runner pulling level with the one ahead
branches.cn: 跑者追平了前面那一个人

intro.en: An Old English noun for a pair, a Latin noun for a wick, their French and English descendants, and three English endings carry the two histories into one modern word.
intro.cn: 一个表示「一对」的古英语名词、一个表示「灯芯」的拉丁语名词、它们在法语与英语里的后代，再加三个英语词尾，把两条历史装进一个现代词。

latinIntro.en: Only the fire sense has a Latin line: myxa, the lamp wick, came through Greek and Old French. The pairing sense is Germanic and has no Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 只有「火柴」这一义项有拉丁线索：myxa（灯芯）经希腊语与古法语传来；「配对」这一义项属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 材料；原料；布料；素材、资料；物质的；重要的、实质性的
definition_en: the stuff from which something is made, cloth, facts used for a work, or being important and physical
core_image: 一匹摊在裁床上的灰蓝布料，剪刀沿粉线往里走，布屑落在木台上
scene: 裁床上的灰蓝布料摊开，剪刀沿粉线往里走，布屑落了一地。The tailor spreads the material and cuts along the chalk line.
sceneCN: 这里 material 指可裁剪缝制的织物（第 2 个义项：做衣服用的布料）；句意：裁缝把布料铺开，沿着粉线裁剪。图中可辨识物件：裁床、灰蓝布料、剪刀、粉线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 材料；原料；布料；素材、资料
物质的；重要的、实质性的

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）
复数（指多种材料或布料）

derivatives.zh: 实质上；在物质方面
物质性；重要性
唯物主义；物质主义
唯物主义者；追逐物质的人
实现；具体化
非物质的；无关紧要的

senses.title: Stuff used to build or make
senses.titleCN: 用来建造或制作的材料
senses.definition: the substance out of which something is made or built
senses.definitionCN: 用来制造或建造某物的物质
senses.example: Bricks and timber were the material of the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 砖与木料是这座老桥的材料。
senses.why: Late Latin materialis was simply the adjective of materia 'stuff', so the noun kept the plain sense of the stuff itself.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁 materialis 就是 materia「材料」的形容词，名词义因此保留了「料本身」这层直白意思。

senses.title: Cloth for sewing
senses.definition: fabric used for making clothes or furnishings
senses.definitionCN: 用来做衣服或家居用品的布料
senses.example: The tailor spread the material and cut along the chalk line.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝把布料铺开，沿粉线裁剪。
senses.why: cloth was the material a household handled most often, so the word narrowed to fabric in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 布料是家庭最常打交道的材料，于是这个词在日常口语中收窄为「织物」。

senses.title: Facts and sources for a work
senses.definition: information, notes or sources used for writing, research or a report
senses.definitionCN: 用于写作、研究或报道的信息、笔记与来源
senses.example: The reporter gathered material for the story over three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 记者用三周时间为这篇报道收集素材。
senses.why: what clay is to a pot, notes are to an article, so the same word covers the raw stuff of a text.
senses.whyCN: 黏土之于陶罐，正如笔记之于文章，于是同一个词也指文本的原料。

senses.title: Supplies and equipment
senses.definition: the things needed for a particular activity, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动所需的物品，通常用复数
senses.example: The laboratory ordered its materials for the autumn term.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室订购了秋季学期要用的用品。
senses.why: in the plural the word counts separate items rather than an uncountable stuff, a shift English makes freely with substances.
senses.whyCN: 复数把不可数的「料」转成一件件可数的东西，英语对物质名词常有这种转换。

senses.title: Physical rather than spiritual
senses.titleCN: 物质层面的，与精神相对
senses.definition: belonging to the physical world rather than to thought or spirit
senses.definitionCN: 属于物理世界，而非思想或精神世界
senses.example: The material world still obeys physical law.
senses.exampleCN: 物质世界依然服从物理规律。
senses.why: the adjective kept the old opposition of stuff to spirit, so it describes whatever can be touched.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了「材料对精神」的古老对举，因此描述一切摸得着的东西。

senses.title: Important to a decision
senses.definition: significant enough to affect a decision, a contract or a judgment
senses.definitionCN: 重要到足以影响决定、合同或判断的
senses.example: The delay was material to the terms of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误对合同条款有实质影响。
senses.why: law and accounting borrowed the word because a fact with real stuff in it can change an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 法律与会计借用这个词，因为有实体内容的事实才足以改变结果。

senses.title: Concerned with wealth
senses.definition: interested in money and possessions rather than in higher aims
senses.definitionCN: 看重金钱与财物而非更高追求
senses.example: They chased material gain and ignored the damage.
senses.exampleCN: 他们追逐物质利益，无视造成的损害。
senses.why: if the material world is what can be touched, then gain in that world is money and goods.
senses.whyCN: 既然物质世界就是摸得着的那一面，那么那一面的收获自然就是钱与物。

senses.title: A person suited to a role
senses.definition: a person considered as suitable raw stuff for a particular post or task
senses.definitionCN: 被看作适合某项职位或任务的「生料」
senses.example: She is good material for the debate team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是辩论队的好苗子。
senses.why: a person is treated as raw stuff to be shaped by training, which keeps the oldest sense of material alive in a comic way.
senses.whyCN: 人被当成可被训练塑造的生料，这以略带戏谑的方式保留了 material 最古老的意思。

intro.en: Material is Late Latin materialis, the adjective of materia 'stuff', which passed through Old French into English. Its parent noun is the same source as matter.
intro.cn: material 是晚期拉丁 materialis，即 materia「材料」的形容词，经古法语进入英语；其母名词与 matter 同源。

items.en: Materia meant timber, stuff and subject matter; the adjective materialis was formed on it in later Latin.
items.cn: materia 指木料、材料与题材；形容词 materialis 是晚期拉丁语在它之上构成的。

items.en: Materialis meant 'of matter, physical' and was used in philosophy to contrast the physical with the spiritual.
items.cn: materialis 意为「物质的、物理的」，在哲学中用来与精神相对。

items.en: Old French material brought the adjective and noun into English in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: 古法语 material 在十三、十四世纪把这个形容词与名词带入英语。

items.en: By the sixteenth century material was the ordinary word for cloth in a household, a sense that still survives in tailoring.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，material 已是家庭里指布料的常用词，这一义至今留在裁缝行当。

items.en: Modern law and accounting use 'material' for facts that can shift a decision, an extension of the idea of having real substance.
items.cn: 现代法律与会计用 material 指能改变决定的事实，这是「有实质」这一想法的延伸。

items.en: First recorded dates for the cloth, legal and accounting senses are approximate; the core adjective is well attested from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 布料义、法律义与会计义的最早记录年代为约数；核心形容词义在十四世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group holds near-forms of material, some sharing its Latin stock and some not; the second group holds words that overlap in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是与 material 形近的词，有的同出拉丁词源，有的不是；第二组是词义部分重叠的词。

entries.definition: The noun and verb built directly on materia; material is its learned adjective, so the two share a root but not a part of speech.
entries.definitionCN: 直接由 materia 构成的名词与动词；material 是它的书面形容词，二者同根而词性不同。

entries.definition: The same word borrowed a second time from French and narrowed to military stores; it is not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词第二次从法语借入，收窄为军用物资；并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: From mater 'mother', not materia; any family resemblance rests on the unproven mater-materia hypothesis.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 mater「母亲」而非 materia；所谓亲缘只建立在那条未获证实的假说上。

entries.definition: The adverb of material, used for 'to a significant degree'; it is a derived form, not a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: material 的副词，表示「达到显著程度」；它是派生形式，不是另一个词。

entries.definition: Material seen as the thing that underlies qualities; substance is more abstract and less countable.
entries.definitionCN: 被看作承载属性的材料；substance 更抽象、更不可数。

entries.definition: Cloth made by weaving; it covers only the textile sense of material.
entries.definitionCN: 织成的布；只覆盖 material 的织物义。

entries.definition: One of the substances combined in a mixture; material is the broader word for what anything is made of.
entries.definitionCN: 混合物中的一种成分；material 是更宽泛的「造物之料」。

entries.definition: Facts that support a conclusion; it overlaps the legal sense of material but not the sense of source material.
entries.definitionCN: 支持结论的事实；与 material 的法律义部分重叠，但不指写作素材。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Materialis is the Latin adjective of materia, so material is literally 'of stuff'.
normal.cn: materialis 是 materia 的拉丁形容词，因此 material 字面上就是「属于材料的」。

normal.en: The family runs material, materially, materiality, materialism and materialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 material、materially、materiality、materialism 与 materialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: raw material, building material, material world.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物质义：原材料、建筑材料、物质世界。

normal.en: In law, a material fact is one that can change the outcome.
normal.cn: 在法律里，具有实质性的关键事实才能改变结果。

normal.en: The same Latin stock gives matter, and material is its adjective.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词源也给出 matter，而 material 是它的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a cutting table where the cloth decides what the coat can become.
abstract.cn: 想象一张裁床，布料本身决定了这件外套能做成什么样。

abstract.en: Picture a potter's hands choosing clay before any shape is attempted.
abstract.cn: 想象陶匠在动手塑形之前先挑泥料。

abstract.en: Picture a folder of notes that a writer keeps beside the blank page.
abstract.cn: 想象作家把一叠笔记放在空白稿纸旁边。

examples.en: Recycled material now accounts for a third of the plant's input.
examples.cn: 回收材料现在占这家工厂投入的三分之一。

examples.en: The committee judged the omission material to the audit.
examples.cn: 委员会认定这处遗漏对审计有实质影响。

examples.en: Course material is posted online before each lecture.
examples.cn: 课程材料在每次讲课前发布到网上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买铁料」——盖房装修先买铁、买料，买的都是材料 → 材料、原料

root: 拉丁 materia「材料、木料」→ 晚期拉丁 materialis（materia 加形容词后缀）「物质的」→ 古法语 material → 英语 material；「布料」「重要」义由「做成东西的料」再引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all treat something as the stuff a thing is made from: bricks for a bridge, cloth for a coat, notes for a story, supplies for a term, the physical world for the spirit, facts for a decision, money for a life, and a person for a post.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物当作「造物之料」：桥的砖、外套的布、报道的笔记、学期的用品、对抗精神的物质世界、影响决定的实据、支撑生活的钱财，以及适合某职位的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth on a cutting table, waiting to become something else.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁床上的一匹布，等着被做成别的什么。

branches.en: THE STOCK ITSELF: raw stuff in bulk, and the same stuff counted out as supplies for a term.
branches.cn: 原料本身：成批的生料，以及按学期点清的同一种用品。

branches.en: THE CLOTH ON THE TABLE: the material a household handles most often is fabric.
branches.cn: 桌上的那匹布：家庭最常打交道的材料就是织物。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL OF A TEXT: notes and sources are clay for a writer's pot.
branches.cn: 文本的料：笔记与来源是作家制陶的黏土。

branches.en: THE TOUCHABLE WORLD AND ITS GAINS: what can be touched, and what can be accumulated from it.
branches.cn: 可触摸的世界及其收获：摸得着的那一面，以及从那一面攒下的东西。

branches.en: STUFF THAT DECIDES: a fact with substance changes a contract, and a person with substance fills a post.
branches.cn: 起决定作用的料：有实质的事实能改动合同，有实质的人能补上职位。

intro.en: Material is one Latin root plus one adjective suffix, and both parts recur across a large English family.
intro.cn: material 由一个拉丁词根加一个形容词后缀构成，这两部分在英语的一大批词里反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin materia gives matter and material; the suffix -alis, through French -al, also shapes manual, editorial and commercial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 materia 衍生 matter 与 material；后缀 -alis 经法语 -al 也构成 manual、editorial 与 commercial。

items.example: The root supplies the picture of raw stuff.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「生料」的画面。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of stuff.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把「材料」变成形容词。

items.example: Material carries both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: material 兼有物质与重要两义。

items.example: The same ending appears in manual and editorial.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾出现在 manual 与 editorial 中。

items.meaning: the quality of being material or significant
items.example: Auditors test materiality before they test figures.
items.exampleCN: 审计师先判断重要性，再核对数字。

items.meaning: the belief that matter is all there is
items.meaningCN: 认为物质即一切的学说
items.example: The suffix turns a quality into a doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把一种性质变成一种主义。

items.example: The design materialized as a real bridge.
items.exampleCN: 设计落实成了一座真实的桥。

items.example: The prefix denies both the stuff and the weight.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀同时否掉「实体」与「分量」。

items.example: A second borrowing narrowed to army stores.
items.exampleCN: 第二次借入的形收窄为军队物资。

definition_zh: 数学；数学课；数学运算
definition_en: the science of numbers, quantities, and shapes, or the school subject that teaches it; informal American English for mathematics
core_image: 黑板上写满数字与公式，一支粉笔正在解题
scene: 铃声响起，同学们收起练习册走向下一间教室。She got the highest score in the class on the math test.
sceneCN: 这里指学校科目「数学」（第 1 个义项：作为学科或科学的数学）；句意为她在全班数学测验中得了最高分。

pos.zh: 数学；数学课（美式口语，为 mathematics 的缩略）

derivatives.zh: math 的完整正式形式，义为「数学」这门学科
由 mathematics 加后缀 -al 构成，义为「数学的；精确的」
由 mathematics 加后缀 -ician（从事者）构成，义为「数学家」

senses.title: The school subject or science of numbers
senses.definition: the study or science of numbers, quantities, shapes, and the relationships between them
senses.definitionCN: 研究数、量、形及其关系的学问，也指学校里教这门知识的课程
senses.example: Math is her favorite subject at school.
senses.exampleCN: 数学是她在学校最喜欢的科目。
senses.why: The word is simply a clipped, informal form of mathematics, so it keeps the full academic meaning in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: math 只是 mathematics 的口语缩略形式，所以完整保留了「数学」这门学科的学术含义，只是在日常口语中更简短随意。

senses.title: A calculation or the act of computing
senses.definition: a calculation or piece of arithmetic, especially in the informal phrase do the math
senses.definitionCN: 指一次计算或算术运算，尤其在口语短语 do the math（算一算）中
senses.example: Do the math: three tickets at ten dollars each is thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 算一算：三张票每张十美元，一共三十美元。
senses.why: Because the subject is about calculating, English naturally extends the word to the act of calculating itself.
senses.whyCN: 由于这门学科的本质就是计算，英语顺势把 math 从「学科」引申为「算一算」这个动作本身，带有让人自己想明白的口吻。

intro.en: Math is a modern English clipping of mathematics, which traces back through Latin and Greek to a root about learning and thinking.
intro.cn: math 是现代英语对 mathematics 的口语截短，后者经拉丁语源自希腊语，本义与「学习、思考」相关。

items.en: The Greek noun mathema meant 'that which is learned', from the verb manthanein 'to learn'; the derived adjective mathematikos referred to what pertains to learning, later especially to mathematical study.
items.cn: 希腊语名词 mathema 意为「所学之物」，来自动词 manthanein（学习）；派生形容词 mathematikos 指与学习有关的，后来专指数学研究。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as mathematicus, and mathematica (a plural noun) named the mathematical sciences, preserving the Greek sense of 'the things worth learning'.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊语形容词作 mathematicus，复数名词 mathematica 用来命名「数学诸学科」，保留了「值得学习的学问」这层希腊语义。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as mathematique, part of the learned vocabulary carried through medieval universities.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语作 mathematique，是中世纪大学学术词汇的一部分。

items.en: Middle English took mathematics from Old French and Latin in the fourteenth century, at first covering all learned sciences before narrowing to the science of numbers.
items.cn: 中古英语在十四世纪经古法语和拉丁语借入 mathematics，最初泛指各门学问，后来才收窄为「数与形的科学」。

items.en: In nineteenth-century American English, mathematics was clipped to maths-style informal forms: Americans favored math while British English favored maths; the clipped form then spread worldwide through American schooling and media.
items.cn: 十九世纪美国英语把 mathematics 截短：美国人偏好 math，英式英语偏好 maths；这一缩略形式随美国教育和传媒传遍世界。

note.en: Words that look or sound close to math, and words that sit near it in meaning.
note.cn: 与 math 拼写或发音相近的词，以及意义相近的词。

entries.definition: the British informal clipping of mathematics, identical in meaning to American math
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语对 mathematics 的口语截短，与美式 math 意思完全相同，只是拼法多了一个 s

entries.definition: the formal, complete name of the science of numbers, quantities, and shapes
entries.definitionCN: math 的完整正式形式，指「数学」这门学科的正式名称，用于书面与正式场合

entries.definition: a tall pole on a ship that holds the sails, only spelled one letter different from math
entries.definitionCN: 船上的桅杆；与 math 仅差一个字母，纯属拼写相近，词源毫无关系

entries.definition: the branch of mathematics dealing with basic counting, adding, subtracting, and multiplying
entries.definitionCN: 算术：数学中处理计数、加减乘等基本运算的分支，范围比 math 窄

entries.definition: the branch of mathematics concerned with points, lines, angles, and shapes
entries.definitionCN: 几何学：数学中研究点、线、角与图形的分支

entries.definition: the branch of mathematics using letters and symbols to represent numbers and quantities
entries.definitionCN: 代数：数学中用字母和符号表示数与量的分支

normalIntro.en: Straightforward memory hooks built from the word's real history and use.
normalIntro.cn: 基于词源与真实用法的直接记忆钩子。

normal.en: math is just mathematics with its tail clipped off, like 'photo' from 'photograph'.
normal.cn: math 就是 mathematics 剪掉尾巴，就像 photo 之于 photograph，学科教名变口语短词。

normal.en: British maths keeps the s, American math drops it: same subject, two flags.
normal.cn: 英式 maths 带 s，美式 math 不带：同一门学科，两种旗号。

normal.en: In the phrase 'do the math', math means the calculating itself.
normal.cn: 在短语 do the math（算一算）里，math 指计算动作本身，让人自己想明白。

normal.en: The Greek root manthanein means 'to learn', so mathematics is literally 'the learning'.
normal.cn: 希腊词根 manthanein 意为「学习」，所以 mathematics 字面上就是「所学之学」。

normal.en: math problem, math test, math class: it always names the school subject first.
normal.cn: math problem、math test、math class：它首先用来命名学校里的数学课与数学题。

abstract.en: Picture a chalkboard crowded with digits, and one letter of 'mathematics' being erased at a time until only 'math' remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一块写满数字的黑板，mathematics 的字母被一个个擦掉，最后只剩 math，越擦越口语。

abstract.en: Hear the bell ring after a math test: the word is short because students want a short word for it.
abstract.cn: 听到数学测验结束的铃声：这个词这么短，正因为学生们想要一个短词来叫它。

abstract.en: See yourself saying 'do the math' with a raised eyebrow, letting numbers do the arguing for you.
abstract.cn: 想象你挑眉说一句「你自己算算」，让数字替你把道理讲完。

examples.en: She got the highest score in the class on the math test.
examples.cn: 她在全班的数学测验中得了最高分。

examples.en: If each ticket costs ten dollars, do the math before you invite five friends.
examples.cn: 如果每张票十美元，邀请五个朋友之前先自己算算账。

examples.en: He is good at math but struggles with writing essays.
examples.cn: 他擅长数学，但写作文很吃力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦斯」——麦子丰收要先「斯」（算）清楚账，数学就是算账的学问。

root: math 来自 mathematics 的口语截短；mathematics 经古法语、拉丁语 mathematica 上溯希腊语 mathema（所学之物），词根 manthanein 意为「学习」，与机械（mechanic）等词无关，属公认来源，无争议。

sensesIntro.en: From the school subject itself to the informal act of working out a calculation.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「数学」这门学科本身，延伸到口语里「算一算」的计算动作，两个义项都围绕数字展开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chalkboard full of numbers
core.cn: 核心意象：写满数字的黑板

branches.en: Numbers grow into a full school subject.
branches.cn: 数字汇聚成一门完整的学校科目，即数学课。

branches.en: The subject in action is a calculation you do.
branches.cn: 学科落到动作上，就是「算一算」这次计算。

branches.en: Both senses serve logic and problem solving.
branches.cn: 两个义项都服务于逻辑推理与解题。

branches.en: Precision is the standard the subject demands.
branches.cn: 精确是这门学科对答案的要求。

branches.en: Doing the math ends an argument with a number.
branches.cn: 算清数字，争论自然结束。

intro.en: Math itself has no separable prefix or suffix, but its family words show how the Greek learning-root built a whole vocabulary.
intro.cn: math 本身不可拆分前后缀，但它的家族词展示了希腊语「学习」词根如何构建一整套数学词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin and Greek relatives that share the learning root.
latinIntro.cn: 共享「学习」词根的拉丁与希腊同族词。

items.meaning: the science of numbers and shapes
items.example: Mathematics is required for the engineering degree.
There is a mathematical proof for the claim.

items.meaningCN: 数学家：数学领域的专家
items.example: The mathematician solved a century-old problem.
items.exampleCN: 这位数学家解决了一个百年难题。

items.example: Physics and economics both end in -ics.
items.exampleCN: physics 和 economics 都以 -ics 结尾。

items.meaning: a person skilled in a field
items.example: A magician is not a mathematician.
Arithmetic comes before algebra in school.
items.exampleCN: 学校里先学算术再学代数。

items.meaningCN: 博学者：通晓多门学问的人
items.exampleCN: 达·芬奇是真正的博学者。

items.meaningCN: 后果；余波（此 math 为古义「收割后的草地」，词源不同）
items.example: The aftermath of the storm left debris everywhere.
items.exampleCN: 风暴过后到处都是残骸。

derivatives.zh: math 的完整正式形式，义为「数学」
由 mathematics 加 -al 构成，义为「数学的；精确的」
由 mathematics 加 -ician 构成，义为「数学家」

definition_zh: 物质；事情；问题；要紧、有关系；【医】脓液
definition_en: the physical stuff that things are made of, an affair under discussion, or to be important
core_image: 一块被雨水泡软的黑泥，手指一捏就能变形，也能弄脏任何碰到它的东西
scene: 泥地刚被雨水浸透，脚一踩就陷下去，鞋底带起黏稠的一团。The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
sceneCN: 这里 matter 指构成物体的有形之物（第 1 个义项：与形式相对、可被感官触及的实体材料）；句意：那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。图中可辨识物件：泥洼、沾泥的靴子、铁锹、水桶；对应第 1 个义项。

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: 就事论事的；不动声色的（由本词与「事实」一词构成的复合形容词）
反物质（加表示「相反」的前缀构成，指电荷相反的物质）
无实质内容的（加表示「没有」的后缀构成）
含脓的（加形容词后缀构成，旧医学用法，现已罕用）

senses.title: Physical substance
senses.definition: the physical substance that occupies space and can be seen or touched
senses.definitionCN: 占据空间、可被看见或摸到的实体材料
senses.example: The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。
senses.why: matter goes back to Latin materia, which meant timber and the stuff a thing is built from, so the physical sense is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: matter 上溯到拉丁 materia，本指木料与造物所用的料，因此「有形之物」是最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: An affair or business
senses.titleCN: 一件待办或已办的事情
senses.definition: a situation, event or piece of business that someone deals with
senses.definitionCN: 某人需要处理的情境、事件或事务
senses.example: She settled a few private matters before leaving for the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 去海边之前，她先处理了几件私事。
senses.why: Latin materia also named the subject under discussion, so the stuff of a talk became the affair itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 materia 也指谈论的题目，于是「谈话的料」就变成了「事情本身」。

senses.title: A problem to be solved
senses.titleCN: 出了差错、需要弄清的问题
senses.definition: a trouble or difficulty, especially one whose cause is not yet known
senses.definitionCN: 麻烦或困难，尤指原因尚未查明的那一种
senses.example: The mechanic asked what the matter was with the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工问发动机出了什么毛病。
senses.why: an affair that has gone wrong is still an affair, so the same word shifted from business to trouble.
senses.whyCN: 出了岔子的事情仍然是一件事情，这个词便从「事务」滑到「麻烦」。

senses.title: To be important
senses.definition: to be of importance or consequence to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事具有重要性或后果
senses.example: Accuracy matters more than speed in this laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 在这间实验室里，准确比速度更要紧。
senses.why: what has substance has weight, and English turned that picture into the verb sense of counting for something.
senses.whyCN: 有实体就有分量，英语把这个画面变成了「算得上数」的动词义。

senses.title: The topic of a text or talk
senses.definition: the subject or content that a piece of writing, speech or study is about
senses.definitionCN: 一篇文章、一段讲话或一项研究所谈论的主题与内容
senses.example: The matter of the lecture was soil chemistry in dry regions.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座的主题是干旱地区的土壤化学。
senses.why: the material of a text is what it carries, and that carrying sense became the topic it treats.
senses.whyCN: 文章的「料」就是它所承载的东西，这一承载义再转为它所处理的主题。

senses.title: Grounds for concern
senses.titleCN: 值得忧虑或申诉的根据
senses.definition: a reason or grounds for a feeling, claim or action
senses.definitionCN: 某种情绪、主张或行动的根据与理由
senses.example: The inspectors found matter for concern in the water samples.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员在采水样中发现了值得忧虑的情况。
senses.why: a matter is something that exists and can be pointed at, so it came to mean a fact solid enough to base a claim on.
senses.whyCN: 事情是存在且指得出的事物，于是引申为「站得住脚、可作依据的事实」。

senses.title: Pus from a wound
senses.definition: the fluid that forms in an infected wound, formerly called matter
senses.definitionCN: 感染伤口中生成的液体，旧时称作 matter
senses.example: The old surgical notes describe the wound discharging matter.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手术记录描述伤口流出脓液。
senses.why: early medicine used matter for any fluid substance of the body, and pus was simply the matter a wound produced.
senses.whyCN: 早期医学用 matter 泛指体内各种液体，脓不过是伤口生成的「物质」。

senses.title: Content as opposed to form
senses.titleCN: 与形式相对的实质内容
senses.definition: the substantive content of a work, as distinct from its style or outward form
senses.definitionCN: 作品的实际内容，与风格或外在形式相对
senses.example: The matter of the essay outweighs its elegant phrasing.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇随笔的内容比它漂亮的措辞更有分量。
senses.why: philosophy opposed matter to form, and literary criticism then asked whether a work had matter behind its shape.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把「质料」与「形式」对举，文学批评随后追问一部作品在形之外有没有实质。

intro.en: Matter came into English through Old French from Latin materia 'timber, stuff, subject'. The common claim that materia derives from mater 'mother' is a hypothesis, not a settled derivation.
intro.cn: matter 经古法语来自拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」。常有人说 materia 由 mater「母亲」派生，那是假说，并非已定的词源。

items.en: Materia meant timber and the material a thing is made from, and by extension the subject of a discussion.
items.cn: materia 指木料以及造物所用的材料，引申为谈论的题目。

items.en: A widely repeated suggestion links materia to mater 'mother', as if the stuff were the mother of the object; this remains a hypothesis and is not established.
items.cn: 一种广为流传的说法把 materia 与 mater「母亲」联系起来，仿佛材料是器物的母亲；这仍属假说，未获证实。

items.en: Old French matere carried both the physical sense and the sense of a subject or affair into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 matere 在诺曼时期之后把「物质」与「题目、事务」两义一并带入英语。

items.en: Middle English matter already covered stuff, a business, a question and grounds for complaint, so the wide sense range is old, not modern.
items.cn: 中古英语的 matter 已兼指物质、事务、问题与申诉的理由，可见义域之宽古已有之，并非现代才有。

items.en: Medical writing of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries used matter for bodily fluid and especially for pus, a use that has since narrowed.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的医学文献用 matter 指体液，尤指脓，这一用法后来收窄。

items.en: The first recorded dates for several senses are approximate; the word itself is well attested from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 若干义项的最早记录年代为约数；这个词本身在十三世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group contains forms that look or sound close to matter but may sit on a different root; the second group contains words that share part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是形或音与 matter 接近、但未必同源的词；第二组是与之部分同义的词。

entries.definition: Built on Latin materialis from materia, so it is the adjective and noun grown from the same stock as matter, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 materialis 构成，而 materialis 出自 materia，因此它是与 matter 同出一源的名词与形容词，并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: A French-shaped doublet of material, borrowed later for military equipment and supplies; it shares the Latin source but not the everyday meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 是 material 的法语式借形词，后借入指军用装备与物资；与 material 同源，但日常义不同。

entries.definition: From Latin mater 'mother' through maternellus; it is related to mater, and only through the unproven mater-materia hypothesis could it be called a cousin of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 经 maternellus 出自拉丁 mater「母亲」；它与 mater 有关，只有借助尚未证实的「母亲—材料」假说，才能算作 matter 的远亲。

entries.definition: From Latin matrix 'womb, mould', built on mater; it names a mould or grid, and does not descend from materia.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 matrix「子宫、模具」，由 mater 构成；它指模具或网格，并非由 materia 传下。

entries.definition: Physical stuff considered as what stands under qualities; matter stresses the material, substance stresses independent existence.
entries.definitionCN: 把物质看作承载属性的基底；matter 强调材料，substance 强调独立存在。

entries.definition: A matter of business or public concern; it covers only the affair sense and never the physical one.
entries.definitionCN: 指事务或公众关注之事；只覆盖「事务」义，绝不指物质。

entries.definition: A topic on which people disagree; it is narrower than matter because it always implies debate.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们有分歧的议题；比 matter 窄，因为它总含争辩之意。

entries.definition: The everyday word for unspecified material; matter is its neutral and technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指未指明材料的日常说法；matter 是它中性、技术化的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin materia first meant timber, so matter is the stuff a thing is built from.
normal.cn: 拉丁 materia 最初指木料，因此 matter 就是造物所用的料。

normal.en: The family runs matter, material, materially, immaterial and materialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 matter、material、materially、immaterial 与 materialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the affair sense: a matter of time, as a matter of fact, no matter what.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出「事情」义：只是时间问题、事实上、无论发生什么。

normal.en: Subject matter keeps the topic sense visible in publishing and teaching.
normal.cn: 「主题素材」这一说法让「主题」义在出版与教学里一直可见。

normal.en: The verb is used in questions of value: it matters, it does not matter.
normal.cn: 动词义出现在价值判断里：这要紧、这不要紧。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of clay that takes the shape of whatever presses into it.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黏土，什么按上去就留下什么形状。

abstract.en: Picture a desk with one folded note on it, and everyone asks about that note first.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上只有一张折起的字条，所有人先问的都是那张字条。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the pan with real goods sinks and the empty pan rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，装了实物的那端沉下去，空的那端翘起来。

examples.en: In legal drafting, the matter of a contract means its operative content rather than its layout.
examples.cn: 在法律起草中，合同的 matter 指其有效内容，而不是排版。

examples.en: Dark matter does not emit light, yet its gravity holds galaxies together.
examples.cn: 暗物质不发光，但它的引力把星系维系在一起。

examples.en: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as the measurements stay exact.
examples.cn: 只要测量保持精确，你走得多慢都不要紧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈特」——妈妈特别在意的那件事，就是要紧的事 → 事情、要紧；妈妈捏的那团泥，就是物质

root: 拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」（一说由 mater「母亲」派生，仅为常见假说）→ 古法语 matere「材料、事务」→ 英语 matter；「问题」与「脓」义由「事情」「体内物质」再引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one lump of stuff: it is the material of things, then the material of talk, then the affair, the trouble inside it, the fact that carries weight, the topic of a text, the fluid in a wound, and finally content set against form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一团「料」辐射出去：先是造物的材料，再是谈话的材料，继而成为事情、事情里的麻烦、有分量的事实、文本的主题、伤口的液体，最后是与形式相对的实质内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of wet clay that can be shaped, weighed and pointed at.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团湿黏土，可被塑形、称重、指认。

branches.en: THE LUMP ITSELF: clay in the yard and pus in a wound are both stuff a body or a boot meets.
branches.cn: 这团东西本身：院里的泥与伤口的脓，都是身体或靴子会碰到的实体。

branches.en: THE AFFAIR AND ITS SNAG: business first, then the trouble discovered inside it.
branches.cn: 事情与其中的疙瘩：先是事务，再是事务里查出的麻烦。

branches.en: WEIGHT THAT COUNTS: what has substance can tip a decision, so matter becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 有分量才算数：有实体就能压动决定，于是 matter 变成动词。

branches.en: STUFF POINTED AT: the material of a text turns into its topic, and a solid fact into grounds.
branches.cn: 被指认的料：文本的材料变成主题，扎实的事实变成依据。

branches.en: CONTENT AGAINST FORM: philosophy keeps the lump as what remains when style is stripped away.
branches.cn: 内容对形式：哲学把那团料保留为剥去风格后剩下的东西。

intro.en: Matter is built on a Latin root that also yields material and immaterial, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: matter 建立在一个拉丁词根上，同一词根还生出 material 与 immaterial，因此这个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin materia supplies matter, material and materialis; mater supplies maternal and matrix, with the materia link remaining a hypothesis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 materia 衍生 matter 与 material 一系；mater 衍生 maternal 与 matrix 一系，而 materia 与 mater 的联系仍属假说。

items.example: The root gives the picture of stuff a thing is built from.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出「造物所用之料」的画面。

items.example: Its link to materia is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.exampleCN: 它与 materia 的联系只是假说，并非已证的派生。

items.example: The adjective suffix turns stuff into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 形容词后缀把「料」变成描述性的词。

items.example: Material keeps both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: material 兼有「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: It also shapes editorial and commercial.
items.exampleCN: 它同样构成 editorial 与 commercial。

items.example: The negation covers both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀同时否掉「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: The plan materialized as a real building.
items.exampleCN: 计划落实成了一座真实的建筑。

items.example: The later borrowing narrowed to army supplies.
items.exampleCN: 后借入的这一形收窄为军队物资。

definition_zh: 可以；可能；（表示祝愿）愿；五月
definition_en: a modal verb used to give or ask for permission, to say that something is possible, or to express a wish, and also the name of the fifth month
core_image: 一扇虚掩的门，门缝里透出光，能不能推开还说不准
scene: 会议室的窗外在下雨，主管把文件合上，抬手指了指门口。You may leave the meeting early if the weather gets worse.
sceneCN: 这里 may 是「可以」（第 1 个义项：表示许可）；句意为如果天气变坏，你可以提前离开会议。图中可辨识物件：合上的文件夹、窗上的雨痕、半开的门。

pos.zh: 可以；可能；愿；用于委婉请求

derivatives.zh: may 的历史过去式，也可单独表示「可能」，语气更弱
由 may 与 be 合并而成，义为「也许」
由名词 might（力量）加 -y 构成，义为「强大的」

senses.title: Used to give or ask for permission
senses.definition: used to say that someone is allowed to do something, or to ask politely for permission
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某人被允许做某事，或礼貌地请求许可
senses.example: You may leave the meeting early if the weather gets worse.
senses.exampleCN: 如果天气变坏，你可以提前离开会议。
senses.why: The Old English verb magan meant to be able, and permission is its everyday result: if you are able and nobody forbids it, you may do it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 magan 意为「有能力」，许可就是它最日常的结果：只要你有能力又无人禁止，你就可以做。

senses.title: Used to say that something is possible
senses.definition: used to say that something is possible but not certain
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事有可能，但并不确定
senses.example: She may be late because the trains are slow tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 她可能会迟到，因为今晚列车开得慢。
senses.why: The same sense of being able turns into speculation: a thing that can happen is a thing that may happen.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「有能力」的意思转成推测：能够发生的事，也就是可能发生的事。

senses.title: Used to express a wish or blessing
senses.definition: used at the beginning of a sentence to express a hope or a blessing
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，用来表达希望或祝福
senses.example: May you both have a long and happy life together.
senses.exampleCN: 愿你们二人白头偕老、生活幸福。
senses.why: A wish is something you want to be able to happen, so Old English put the verb of ability first to voice a blessing.
senses.whyCN: 愿望就是你希望「能够发生」的事，所以古英语把表示「能够」的动词提到句首，用来表达祝福。

senses.title: The fifth month of the year
senses.definition: the fifth month of the year, written with a capital letter
senses.definitionCN: 一年的第五个月，书写时首字母大写
senses.example: May is the month when the garden finally turns green.
senses.exampleCN: 五月是花园终于变绿的那个月份。
senses.why: The month name comes from Latin Maius, named after a Roman goddess; it shares spelling with the modal but not its history.
senses.whyCN: 月份名来自拉丁语 Maius，以罗马女神命名；它与情态动词拼写相同，来历却完全不同。

intro.en: The modal may goes back to an Old English verb of ability, while the month May comes from a Latin god's name; the two only happen to be spelled alike.
intro.cn: 情态动词 may 来自古英语中表示「有能力」的动词，而月份 May 来自拉丁语神名；两者只是碰巧拼写相同。

items.en: A reconstructed root often written meg- or magh- is thought to carry the sense of being able or having power.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构词根（常写作 meg- 或 magh-）带有「有能力、有力量」的意思。

items.en: Old English magan meant to be able or to have power, and it was already a defective verb without an ordinary infinitive.
items.cn: 古英语 magan 意为「能够、有力量」，当时已是缺少普通不定式的残缺动词。

items.en: Its present forms ran mæg and magon, and its past was meahte, shapes that survived into modern English.
items.cn: 它的现在时形式有 mæg、magon，过去式是 meahte，这些形式一直活到现代英语。

items.en: Middle English kept may and might, and the pair began to split between present permission and past or tentative possibility.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了 may 与 might，这一对开始分工：前者表现在的许可，后者表过去或委婉的可能。

items.en: Modern English uses may for permission, possibility and blessings, and writes the month May with a capital letter from Latin Maius.
items.cn: 现代英语用 may 表示许可、可能和祝愿；月份 May 首字母大写，来自拉丁语 Maius。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the modal's old forms and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of saying possible or allowed.
note.cn: 形近组收这个情态动词的旧形式与复合词；近义组收其他表示「可能」或「被允许」的说法。

entries.definition: The historical past tense of may, now also a weaker word for possibility.
entries.definitionCN: may 的历史过去式，如今也单独表示较弱的可能性。

entries.definition: Perhaps; a single word built from may and be.
entries.definitionCN: 也许；由 may 与 be 合并而成的一个词。

entries.definition: The Old English verb meaning to be able, the ancestor of may.
entries.definitionCN: 古英语动词，意为「能够」，是 may 的祖先。

entries.definition: Strong and powerful, built on the noun might meaning strength.
entries.definitionCN: 强大的；由表示力量的名词 might 加后缀构成。

entries.definition: Used for ability or permission, often more direct than may.
entries.definitionCN: 表示能力或许可，通常比 may 直接。

entries.definition: The past of can, and a politer or more tentative form.
entries.definitionCN: can 的过去式，也是更客气、更不确定的说法。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning possibly, close to the speculative use of may.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「也许」，接近 may 的推测用法。

entries.definition: Permitted by a rule or by a person in charge.
entries.definitionCN: 被规则或负责人允许的。

normalIntro.en: The modal is an old verb of ability worn down to three letters, and the month beside it is a Latin name that only looks the same.
normalIntro.cn: 这个情态动词是磨得只剩三个字母的古老「能力」动词，而旁边那个月份只是长得一样的拉丁名字。

normal.en: Magan in Old English meant to be able, so may began as a word about capacity rather than permission.
normal.cn: 古英语 magan 意为「能够」，所以 may 起初是讲能力的词，而不是讲许可的。

normal.en: Its past tense meahte became might, which is why might still sounds like a softer may.
normal.cn: 它的过去式 meahte 变成 might，所以 might 至今听起来像一个语气更软的 may。

normal.en: Maybe is simply may plus be written as one word, a compressed way of saying it may be so.
normal.cn: maybe 就是 may 与 be 合成一个词，是「it may be so」的压缩说法。

normal.en: May well means there is good reason to think so, while may as well means there is no better choice.
normal.cn: may well 意为「有充分理由这样想」，may as well 意为「没有更好的选择」。

normal.en: The month May is capitalized because it is a proper name from Latin Maius, not the modal verb.
normal.cn: 月份 May 首字母大写，因为它是来自拉丁语 Maius 的专名，而不是这个情态动词。

abstract.en: Think of a half-open door: you are able to push it, but whether you should is another question.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇半开的门：你有能力推开，但该不该推是另一回事。

abstract.en: A forecast saying it may rain is a sentence standing between yes and no.
abstract.cn: 预报说可能下雨，就是一句停在「是」与「否」之间的话。

abstract.en: The same letters name a month and a mood of possibility; English lets spelling hide two separate histories.
abstract.cn: 同样的字母既是一个月份，也是一种可能语气；英语就让拼写掩盖了两段不同的来历。

examples.en: You may leave the meeting early if the weather gets worse.
examples.cn: 如果天气变坏，你可以提前离开会议。

examples.en: She may be late because the trains are slow tonight.
examples.cn: 她可能会迟到，因为今晚列车开得慢。

examples.en: May you both have a long and happy life together.
examples.cn: 愿你们二人白头偕老、生活幸福。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「没」——有没有把握说不准，所以 may 是「可能」；问人可不可以，也用 may。

root: 古英语 magan（能够、有力量）的现在式 mæg 演变而来，过去式 meahte 成为 might；月份 May 另出自拉丁语 Maius，与此词没有词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: The core is ability turning into possibility; permission is the everyday side of that ability, the wish is its optative use, and the month is a separate Latin name.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「能力」转为「可能」；许可是这种能力最日常的一面，祝愿是它的祈愿用法，而月份则是另一个拉丁名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door standing ajar, able to be pushed but not yet pushed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇虚掩的门，推得开，却还没有推。

branches.en: an open door with a hand resting on the frame
branches.cn: 一扇开着的门，一只手搭在门框上

branches.en: a sky that could rain or could clear
branches.cn: 一片可能下雨也可能放晴的天

branches.en: a sign saying that visitors are permitted
branches.cn: 一块写着访客获准进入的牌子

branches.en: a toast raised at a wedding
branches.cn: 婚礼上举起的一杯酒

branches.en: a garden turning green in the fifth month
branches.cn: 花园在第五个月转绿

intro.en: The word is an Old English verb of ability worn down to three letters, with a compound and a past form built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词是古英语中表示「能够」的动词，磨得只剩三个字母，并用同一词干造出一个复合词和一个过去式。

latinIntro.en: The modal verb has no reliable Latin cognate, since it descends from Old English; only the month name May goes back to Latin Maius.
latinIntro.cn: 这个情态动词没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因为它源自英语本土；只有月份名 May 可上溯到拉丁语 Maius。

items.meaning: to be able, to have power
items.exampleCN: magan 是 may 的古英语原形。

items.meaning: first and third person singular of magan
items.meaningCN: magan 的第一、第三人称单数
items.exampleCN: mæg 是 magan 的现在式单数形式。
meahte 是 magan 的过去式。
-an 标出 magan 的不定式身份。

items.meaningCN: may 的过去式；也可指力量
items.exampleCN: might 由 meahte 演变而来。
may 是磨短之后的现代形式。
maybe 由 may 与 be 合并而成。
be 是 maybe 的后半部分。

latinEntries.meaning: of May, belonging to the month of May

definition_zh: 也许；可能；（口语）或许吧；不确定的事
definition_en: used to say that something is possible but not certain, or to make a gentle suggestion, and informally a thing that is still undecided
core_image: 天平两端各放一枚砝码，还在轻轻摇晃，没有落定
scene: 两个人站在站台上，雨云压得很低，列车时刻牌迟迟不翻。Maybe the rain will stop before we reach the station.
sceneCN: 这里 maybe 是「也许」（第 1 个义项：表示不确定的可能）；句意为也许我们到站之前雨就会停。图中可辨识物件：站台、时刻牌、压低的雨云。

pos.zh: （口语）不确定的事；悬而未决的事

derivatives.zh: maybe 的前半部分，表示「可能」，来自古英语 magan
与 may 同源的历史过去式，也可表示较弱的可能
maybe 的后半部分，来自古英语表示「是、存在」的动词

senses.title: Used to say something is possible but not certain
senses.definition: used when you think something is possible, without saying that it is certain
senses.definitionCN: 在你认为某事有可能、但不确定时使用
senses.example: Maybe the rain will stop before we reach the station.
senses.exampleCN: 也许我们到站之前雨就会停。
senses.why: The word is may plus be: a compressed sentence saying it may be so, with the doubt of may kept inside.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 may 加 be，把一个意为「或许如此」的句子压缩起来，may 那点不确定感也留在里面。

senses.title: Used to make a gentle suggestion
senses.definition: used in speech to suggest a course of action without sounding like an order
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来提出某个做法，又不像在下命令
senses.example: Maybe we should call her before we drive over.
senses.exampleCN: 也许我们该在开车过去之前给她打个电话。
senses.why: A suggestion phrased with maybe leaves the decision open, so the same doubt becomes a polite way of proposing.
senses.whyCN: 用 maybe 提出的建议把决定权留开，于是同一份不确定就变成了客气地提议。

senses.title: A hesitant answer that agrees without promising
senses.definition: used alone as an answer that neither accepts nor refuses
senses.definitionCN: 单独用作回答，既不答应也不拒绝
senses.example: Will you come to the reunion? Maybe.
senses.exampleCN: 你会来聚会吗？或许吧。
senses.why: Because maybe marks an open possibility, a bare maybe as an answer lets the speaker stay uncommitted.
senses.whyCN: 因为 maybe 标出的是一种开放的可能，单独用它作答，说话人就不必作出承诺。

senses.title: Something that is still undecided
senses.definition: an informal noun for a plan or result that is not settled yet
senses.definitionCN: 非正式的名词，指尚未定下来的计划或结果
senses.example: The trip is still a maybe until the tickets are booked.
senses.exampleCN: 在机票订好之前，这趟旅行还说不准。
senses.why: Once maybe names a possibility, it can be turned into a noun for the thing that sits in that doubtful state.
senses.whyCN: 既然 maybe 指的是一种可能性，它就能被当作名词，指处在那种不确定状态里的事情。

intro.en: Maybe is an English compound rather than a borrowed word: may came from an Old English verb of ability, be from the verb of existence, and the two were written as one word in Middle English.
intro.cn: maybe 是英语本土的复合词，不是借词：may 来自古英语表示「能够」的动词，be 是表示存在的动词，两者在中古英语时期合并成一个词。

items.en: Magan meant to be able, and its present stem supplied may as the word for possibility.
items.cn: magan 意为「能够」，它的现在时词干提供了表示可能性的 may。

items.en: Beon meant to be or to exist, and it is the source of modern be in all its irregular forms.
items.cn: beon 意为「是、存在」，是现代 be 及其各种不规则形式的来源。

items.en: The two words stood side by side as may be, a clause meaning it may be so.
items.cn: 这两个词在中古英语中并排出现，写作 may be，是一个意为「或许如此」的小句。

items.en: By the late medieval period the pair was written as one word and used like an adverb.
items.cn: 到中古英语后期，这一对已被写成一个词，并像副词一样使用。

items.en: Modern English uses maybe freely in speech and informal writing, beside perhaps in more formal styles.
items.cn: 现代英语在口语和非正式写作中自由使用 maybe，较正式文体则常用 perhaps。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the parts and close neighbours of the compound; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的组成部分与近邻；近义组收其他表示可能性的副词。

entries.definition: The modal verb meaning can or possibly will, the front half of maybe.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，意为「可以」或「可能」，是 maybe 的前半部分。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to exist or to be, the back half of maybe.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「是、存在」的动词，是 maybe 的后半部分。

entries.definition: The past form of may, also used for weaker possibility.
entries.definitionCN: may 的过去式，也用来表示较弱的可能性。

entries.definition: A verb phrase meaning it is possible that it is, written as two words.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，意为「可能是」，写作两个词。

entries.definition: A more formal adverb for possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 表示可能性的较正式副词。

entries.definition: An adverb saying that something could happen or be true.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事可能发生或属实的副词。

entries.definition: An adverb saying something is likely, stronger than maybe.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事很可能，语气比 maybe 强。

entries.definition: Used when you suppose something is true from the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 根据证据推断某事属实时使用。

normalIntro.en: The word is two short verbs fused, and its meaning is the doubt that may brings to the plain verb be.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由两个短动词熔合而成，意思就是 may 带给 be 的那点不确定。

normal.en: Maybe is may plus be, so the word literally contains the sentence it may be.
normal.cn: maybe 是 may 加 be，字面上就装着「it may be」这句话。

normal.en: May started as an Old English verb of ability, which is why maybe carries possibility rather than certainty.
normal.cn: may 起初是古英语中表示能力的动词，所以 maybe 带的是可能而非确定。

normal.en: Written as two words, may be is a verb phrase; written as one, maybe is an adverb.
normal.cn: 写成两个词时 may be 是动词短语，写成一个词时 maybe 是副词。

normal.en: Maybe not and maybe so are the two easiest pairs to remember, one closing and one opening the possibility.
normal.cn: maybe not 与 maybe so 是最容易记的两对，一个关上一个打开可能性。

normal.en: A big maybe is the informal noun use, for something still undecided.
normal.cn: a big maybe 是它的非正式名词用法，指还悬着的事。

abstract.en: Picture two coins still swinging on a balance, never settling on one side.
abstract.cn: 想象天平上两枚硬币还在晃，始终不落向一边。

abstract.en: Saying maybe is like leaving a door half open so that either answer can walk in.
abstract.cn: 说 maybe 就像把门留半开，让哪个答案都能走进来。

abstract.en: Two short verbs joined into one word show how English compresses a whole hesitant sentence into a few sounds.
abstract.cn: 两个短动词并成一个词，正好显示英语如何把一整句犹豫的话压成很少的音节。

examples.en: Maybe the rain will stop before we reach the station.
examples.cn: 也许我们到站之前雨就会停。

examples.en: Maybe we should call her before we drive over.
examples.cn: 也许我们该在开车过去之前给她打个电话。

examples.en: The trip is still a maybe until the tickets are booked.
examples.cn: 在机票订好之前，这趟旅行还说不准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「妹比」——妹妹和别人比，谁更好还说不准；记住 maybe 是「也许」。

root: 由古英语 magan（能够）演变来的 may 与古英语 beon（是、存在）演变来的 be 合并而成；中古英语后期写成一词，作副词使用。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an open possibility; from it come the plain adverb, the polite suggestion, the hesitant answer, and the informal noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个开放的可能性；由此分出普通副词用法、客气建议、含糊回答，以及非正式的名词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance still swinging, with neither side yet resting on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平还在轻晃，两端都没有落到桌上。

branches.en: a forecast that keeps both options open
branches.cn: 一份把两种可能都留着的天气预报

branches.en: a hand raised before anyone starts driving
branches.cn: 还没发动车子前抬起的一只手

branches.en: a bare maybe given to a question
branches.cn: 对一个问题只回一句「或许吧」

branches.en: a plan sitting on the table without a date
branches.cn: 摊在桌上却没有日期的计划

branches.en: a word that turns doubt into something you can hold
branches.cn: 一个把犹豫变成可以拿在手里的东西的词

intro.en: The word is two Old English verbs welded together, and both pieces still show in the spelling.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个古英语动词焊在一起，两个部件在拼写里仍然看得见。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word, which is an English compound of two Old English verbs.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它是由两个古英语动词构成的英语复合词。

items.exampleCN: magan 是 may 的古英语原形。
may 是 magan 磨短后的现在形式。
beon 是现代 be 的古英语来源。
be 是 maybe 的后半部分。
maybe 由两个词合并而成。
might 与 may 同出一源。
-an 标出 magan 的不定式身份。

items.meaningCN: be 的一个现在式形式
items.exampleCN: is 是 be 的一个现在式形式。

definition_zh: 我（宾格）；我（作介词宾语）；我（作表语）；我（口语作主语）
definition_en: the pronoun a speaker uses for himself or herself when it is the object of a verb or preposition, and in a few other positions in informal English
core_image: 说话人把手按在自己胸口，向对面的人指一下自己
scene: 雨夜里公交站只剩两个人，陌生人把伞往这边递过来。Could you share the umbrella with me until the bus comes?
sceneCN: 这里是「介词后的宾格」（第 2 个义项：作介词宾语）；句意为能否把伞与我共用到公交车来。图中可辨识物件：雨伞、站牌、湿漉漉的地面。

pos.zh: 我（宾格；口语中也可作主语或表语）

derivatives.zh: 由 me 加 -self 构成的反身代词，义为「我自己」
与 me 同属第一人称代词体系的名词性物主代词，义为「我的东西」
与 me 同源的第一人称物主限定词，义为「我的」

senses.title: The object of a verb
senses.definition: the pronoun a speaker uses when referring to himself or herself as the direct or indirect object of a verb
senses.definitionCN: 说话人指自己、充当动词直接或间接宾语时用的代词
senses.example: The teacher asked me a difficult question.
senses.exampleCN: 老师问了我一个难题。
senses.why: Old English kept a separate accusative form mē for the object role, so the pronoun changes shape the moment it stops being the subject.
senses.whyCN: 古英语为宾语角色保留了独立的宾格形式 mē，所以这个代词一旦不做主语就得换形，me 正是那套格变化留下的宾语形态。

senses.title: The object of a preposition
senses.definition: the pronoun used after a preposition when the speaker is the thing the preposition points to
senses.definitionCN: 介词之后使用、表示介词所指向的说话人本身的代词
senses.example: This letter is addressed to me.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信是寄给我的。
senses.why: Old English prepositions governed the dative, and the same mē served both object cases, which is why one short form now covers every preposition.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的介词支配与格，而同一个 mē 同时承担两种宾语格，所以今天一个短形式就能跟在所有介词后面。

senses.title: The complement after be
senses.definition: the pronoun used after a linking verb or in a comparison, where older grammar once expected the subject form
senses.definitionCN: 连系动词之后或比较句中使用的代词，旧语法在此处本要求用主格
senses.example: It was me at the door, not my brother.
senses.exampleCN: 在门口的是我，不是我弟弟。
senses.why: After be the pronoun is felt as the point of focus rather than the doer, so the object form survives where Latin-based rules would still ask for the subject form.
senses.whyCN: 在 be 之后，代词被感知为被指出的焦点而不是动作发出者，因此在依拉丁规则本该用主格的位置，宾格形式反而留了下来。

senses.title: The subject in informal speech
senses.definition: the pronoun used as part of the subject in casual speech, especially when it is joined to another noun by and
senses.definitionCN: 随意口语中充当主语一部分的代词，尤指与另一个名词用 and 并列时
senses.example: Me and my cousin run a small shop.
senses.exampleCN: 我和我表弟经营一家小店。
senses.why: In relaxed speech the pronoun is treated as one unmarked word rather than as a case form, so me spreads into the subject slot that school grammar reserves for I.
senses.whyCN: 在随意的口语里，代词被当成一个不带格标记的词，于是 me 扩散到学校语法留给 I 的主语位置。

intro.en: Me is the old object form of the first person pronoun, and it descends from a root shared by Latin and English.
intro.cn: me 是第一人称代词古老的宾语形式，其词根为拉丁语与英语所共有。

items.en: A reconstructed first person root *me- supplied the oblique forms of the pronoun in many branches of the family.
items.cn: 重构的第一人称词根 *me- 为这一语族许多分支提供了代词的斜格形式。

items.en: The accusative *mek and the dative *miz stood behind the single Old English form that English later kept.
items.cn: 宾格 *mek 与与格 *miz 共同支撑了古英语那个后来被英语保留下来的单一形式。

items.en: Old English mē served as both accusative and dative of ic, the word for I.
items.cn: 古英语 mē 同时充当 ic（我）的宾格与与格。

items.en: Middle English kept me while the old case system slowly broke down and word order took over the work of marking roles.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了 me，同时旧的格系统逐渐瓦解，标记句子角色的工作转由词序承担。

items.en: Modern English uses me for every object role and, informally, for subjects and complements as well.
items.cn: 现代英语用 me 承担所有宾语角色，口语中还扩展到主语与表语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the other forms of the same pronoun paradigm; the near-meaning group collects pronouns that also point at a person.
note.cn: 形近组收同一代词体系里的其他形式；近义组收同样指向某个人称的代词。

entries.definition: The subject form of the same first person pronoun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一第一人称代词的主格形式。

entries.definition: The possessive determiner built on the same pronoun stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同一代词词干上的物主限定词。

entries.definition: The possessive pronoun standing for something that belongs to the speaker.
entries.definitionCN: 表示属于说话者之物的物主代词。

entries.definition: The Latin pronoun for me, from the same reconstructed first person root.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「我」的宾格代词，出自同一重构的第一人称词根。

entries.definition: The object form of we, used when the speaker is part of a group.
entries.definitionCN: we 的宾格，说话人属于一个群体时使用。

entries.definition: A reflexive pronoun referring back to a general person.
entries.definitionCN: 回指泛指的「自己」的反身代词。

entries.definition: The self as consciously perceived, especially in psychology.
entries.definitionCN: 心理学中自觉意识到的「自我」。

normalIntro.en: The word survives from a pronoun paradigm that once marked case on every form; its nearest relatives are the other first person forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自一套曾为每个形式标格的代词体系，它最近的亲属就是第一人称的其他形式。

normal.en: Old English had ic for the subject and mē for the object, and English kept the second form as me.
normal.cn: 古英语用 ic 作主语、mē 作宾语，英语把后者留成了 me。

normal.en: The same m- stem runs through my, mine and myself, so all of them point back to the speaker.
normal.cn: 同一个 m- 词干贯穿 my、mine 与 myself，它们都指回说话人。

normal.en: Latin mē is the same pronoun, so the resemblance is not a coincidence but a shared inheritance.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mē 是同一个代词，所以这种相似不是巧合，而是共同的继承。

normal.en: After a preposition English almost always wants me rather than I, because the object case survived longest there.
normal.cn: 在介词后面英语几乎总是用 me 而不是 I，因为宾格在那里存留得最久。

normal.en: Excuse me is a fixed phrase, so the object form stays even though no verb follows it.
normal.cn: excuse me 是固定短语，所以后面没有动词时也仍然用宾格形式。

abstract.en: Think of me as the version of I that other people can act upon: it appears when something is done to the speaker.
abstract.cn: 把 me 想成可以被别人施加动作的那个 I：当有事情落到说话人身上时，它就出现。

abstract.en: A pronoun is a placeholder, and me is the smallest label a speaker can attach to a body in a room.
abstract.cn: 代词是占位符，而 me 是说话人能贴到房间里某具身体上的最小标签。

abstract.en: A single letter m carries the speaker across languages, from English me to Latin mē.
abstract.cn: 一个字母 m 就把说话人带过语言的边界，从英语 me 到拉丁语 mē。

examples.en: The teacher asked me a difficult question.
examples.cn: 老师问了我一个难题。

examples.en: This parcel is for me, not for my sister.
examples.cn: 这个包裹是给我的，不是给我妹妹的。
