examples.en: It was me who forgot the keys.
examples.cn: 忘带钥匙的是我。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「密」——把嘴凑近说「密」，说的正是自己；记住 me 是「我」。

root: 古英语 mē，是 ic（我）的宾格与与格形式，出自原始日耳曼语 *mek／*miz，更早可追溯到原始印欧语第一人称词根 *me-；拉丁语 mē 为同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the speaker as the target of an action; the senses then spread to prepositions, to the position after be, and to casual subjects.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是作为动作对象的说话人；义项由此扩展到介词之后、be 之后，以及随意的口语主语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a speaker pressing a hand to the chest and pointing at himself.
core.cn: 核心意象：说话人把手按在胸口，向对面的人指一下自己。

branches.en: a hand passing a note to the speaker
branches.cn: 有人把纸条递到说话人手里

branches.en: two voices trading places in a casual sentence
branches.cn: 随口说话时两个人称互相换位

branches.en: a finger pointing at the chest after the door opens
branches.cn: 门开了，手指点在自己胸口

branches.en: the same word on both sides of a verb
branches.cn: 同一个词出现在动词两侧

branches.en: friends talking over each other at a table
branches.cn: 朋友们在桌边抢着说话

intro.en: The word is a single case form from an old pronoun paradigm, supported by the other first person forms and by the reflexive suffix -self.
intro.cn: 这个词是古老代词体系里的一个格形式，由第一人称的其他形式和反身后缀 -self 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pronoun mē belongs to the same first person root, so it is a true cognate rather than a borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语代词 mē 属于同一第一人称词根，是真正的同源词而非借词。

definition_zh: 一餐；一顿饭；饭食；粗粉；谷物磨成的粉
definition_en: an occasion when food is eaten, the food served at that occasion, or grain ground into a coarse powder
core_image: 木桌上摆着一只碗和一袋磨好的谷物粉，吃饭与磨粉落在同一幅画面里
scene: 清晨的厨房里，母亲把燕麦倒进锅里，孩子已经坐在桌边等。We usually have a quiet meal before the school bus arrives.
sceneCN: 这里是「一餐、一顿饭」（第 1 个义项：吃饭的场合）；句意为校车到来之前，我们通常安静地吃一顿饭。图中可辨识物件：锅、燕麦、木桌、碗。

derivatives.zh: 由 meal 与 time 复合而成，义为「用餐时间」
由 meal 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「粉状的；发白的」
由 oat 与 meal（粗粉）复合而成，义为「燕麦片」
由 corn 与 meal（粗粉）复合而成，义为「玉米粗粉」

senses.title: An occasion when food is eaten
senses.definition: a fixed or usual occasion on which a person sits down and eats food
senses.definitionCN: 一个人固定或惯常坐下来吃饭的场合
senses.example: We sat down to a quiet meal at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 我们七点坐下来安静地吃了一顿饭。
senses.why: Old English mǣl first meant a measured or appointed time, so a meal was originally the hour set aside for eating rather than the food itself.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mǣl 本指量好、约定的时间，所以 meal 最初是吃饭被安排的那个时刻，而不是食物本身。

senses.title: The food eaten at such an occasion
senses.definition: the food that is served and eaten at one sitting
senses.definitionCN: 一次坐下用餐时所端上并被吃掉的食物
senses.example: She cooked a simple meal of rice and vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了一顿简单的米饭加蔬菜。
senses.why: Once the appointed hour had a name, the word slid from the time to what filled that time, namely the food on the table.
senses.whyCN: 一旦那个约定的时刻有了名字，词义就从时间滑向填满这段时间的东西，也就是桌上的食物。

senses.title: Grain ground into coarse powder
senses.definition: grain, especially oats or corn, ground coarsely rather than into fine flour
senses.definitionCN: 尤指燕麦或玉米磨得较粗、而非磨成细面粉的谷物
senses.example: The mill turns oats into meal for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 磨坊把燕麦磨成粗粉，留着过冬。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different Old English word, melu, meaning flour; the two words fell together in spelling and now share one entry.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自另一个古英语词 melu，意为面粉；两个词在拼写上合流，如今共用一个词条。

senses.title: Any coarsely ground product used as feed or fertilizer
senses.definition: a powdered product made by grinding bones, fish or shells, used as animal feed or fertilizer
senses.definitionCN: 把骨头、鱼或贝壳磨成粉、用作饲料或肥料的产品
senses.example: Bone meal is spread on the field before planting.
senses.exampleCN: 种植前把骨粉撒在田里。
senses.why: The grinding image at the heart of the flour sense extends easily to bones, fish and shells once industry needs a word for powdered additives.
senses.whyCN: 面粉义项核心的「磨碎」意象很容易延伸到骨头、鱼和贝壳，只要工业需要一个词来称粉末状的添加物。

intro.en: Meal is two Old English words that look alike today: one for an appointed time, one for ground grain.
intro.cn: meal 其实是两个古英语词，今天看起来一样：一个指约定的时间，一个指磨碎的谷物。

items.en: The noun *mēlą meant a measure or a marked point of time, and it is the ancestor of the repast sense.
items.cn: 名词 *mēlą 意为尺度或标出的时间点，是「一餐」这一义项的祖先。

items.en: Old English mǣl named an appointed time and later the meal eaten at that time.
items.cn: 古英语 mǣl 指约定的时刻，后来也指那个时刻吃的那顿饭。

items.en: A separate word, melu, meant flour or grain ground fine, and it is the ancestor of the powder sense.
items.cn: 另一个词 melu 意为面粉或磨细的谷物，是「粗粉」义项的祖先。

items.en: Middle English spelled both words close to mele, and they gradually merged into one form.
items.cn: 中古英语把两个词都写成接近 mele 的形式，二者逐渐合并成一个词形。

items.en: Modern English keeps both senses in one entry and builds compounds such as oatmeal and cornmeal.
items.cn: 现代英语把两个义项收在同一词条里，并构成 oatmeal、cornmeal 等复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the powder family and its mill; the near-meaning group gathers words for a sitting at the table and for ground grain.
note.cn: 形近组收「粉」这一族词和它的磨坊；近义组收表示围桌用餐的词与表示磨碎谷物的词。

entries.definition: Like meal or covered with meal; also used of dry, pale food.
entries.definitionCN: 像粗粉的、覆着粉的；也形容食物干而发白。

entries.definition: The time when a meal is normally eaten.
entries.definitionCN: 通常吃饭的时间。

entries.definition: Oats ground into meal, or the porridge made from them.
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦磨成的粗粉，或由此煮成的粥。

entries.definition: A building or machine that grinds grain.
entries.definitionCN: 磨谷的厂房或机器；磨坊。

entries.definition: The main meal of the day, usually in the evening.
entries.definitionCN: 一天中的正餐，通常指晚餐。

entries.definition: A meal, especially a formal or leisurely one.
entries.definitionCN: 一餐，尤指正式或从容的一顿。

entries.definition: A small amount of food eaten between meals.
entries.definitionCN: 两餐之间吃的一点食物。

entries.definition: Fine powder made by grinding grain, finer than meal.
entries.definitionCN: 谷物磨成的细粉，比粗粉更细。

normalIntro.en: One spelling now holds two histories: a measured hour and a handful of ground grain.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个拼写如今装着两段历史：量出的时刻与一把磨碎的谷物。

normal.en: Old English mǣl meant an appointed time, so the earliest meal was a moment on the clock rather than a plate of food.
normal.cn: 古英语 mǣl 意为约定的时刻，所以最早的 meal 是钟表上的一个时刻，而不是一盘食物。

normal.en: The flour sense comes from melu, a different Old English word that later merged with mǣl in spelling.
normal.cn: 「粉」的义项来自 melu，一个后来在拼写上并入 mǣl 的另一个古英语词。

normal.en: Mealtime and oatmeal are compounds: one adds time, the other adds the grain that was ground.
normal.cn: mealtime 与 oatmeal 都是复合词：一个加上时间，一个加上被磨碎的谷物。

normal.en: The adjective mealy adds -y to meal, giving the idea of something powdery on the surface.
normal.cn: 形容词 mealy 在 meal 后加 -y，表示表面有粉末状的东西。

normal.en: Cornmeal and oatmeal keep the old powder sense alive in kitchens today.
normal.cn: cornmeal 与 oatmeal 让古老的粉末义项至今仍活在厨房里。

abstract.en: A meal is a clock and a table at once: time measured out, then filled with food.
abstract.cn: 一餐既是钟也是桌：先把时间量出来，再用食物把它填满。

abstract.en: Two words that once meant different things can end up spelled the same, and a dictionary entry quietly holds both.
abstract.cn: 两个原本意思不同的词可能最终拼写相同，而一个词条会安静地把二者都收下。

abstract.en: Grinding turns hard grain into soft powder, which is why the same word can name a dinner and a bag of feed.
abstract.cn: 磨碎把坚硬的谷物变成软粉，所以同一个词既能称一顿饭，也能称一袋饲料。

examples.en: We usually have a quiet meal before the school bus arrives.
examples.cn: 校车到来之前，我们通常安静地吃一顿饭。

examples.en: She cooked a simple meal of rice and vegetables.
examples.cn: 她做了一顿简单的米饭加蔬菜。

examples.en: The old mill still grinds corn into meal.
examples.cn: 那座老磨坊仍把玉米磨成粗粉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米了」——米下锅了，就该吃饭；记住 meal 是一餐，也是磨出来的粗粉。

root: 表示「一餐」的义项来自古英语 mǣl（约定的时刻），出自原始日耳曼语 *mēlą；表示「粗粉」的义项来自古英语 melu（面粉），与 mill 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is food at a set time; the senses then split between the occasion, the food, the ground grain and industrial powders.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是按时吃的那顿饭；义项由此分成吃饭的场合、食物本身、磨碎的谷物与工业粗粉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl on a wooden table beside a sack of ground grain.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桌上一只碗，旁边是一袋磨好的谷物粉。

branches.en: a clock marking the hour set aside for eating
branches.cn: 钟表指向专门留给吃饭的时刻

branches.en: a table filled with rice and vegetables
branches.cn: 摆着米饭和蔬菜的饭桌

branches.en: oats falling from the millstone into a sack
branches.cn: 燕麦从磨盘落进布袋

branches.en: bone meal scattered across a field
branches.cn: 骨粉撒在田里

branches.en: a family arriving and sitting down together
branches.cn: 一家人到齐后一起坐下

intro.en: The entry is held together by a Germanic time word, a Germanic flour word, and a handful of English compounds and suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词条由日耳曼语的时间词、日耳曼语的面粉词，以及若干英语复合词与后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Neither Germanic word behind meal has a reliable Latin cognate; Latin molere belongs to the grinding family but is not the source of this word.
latinIntro.cn: meal 背后的两个日耳曼词都没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语 molere 属「磨」的词族，却不是这个词的来源。

definition_zh: 意思是；意味着；打算；平均值；中间值；刻薄的；吝啬的
definition_en: to intend or signify something; also the middle value of a set of numbers, or unkind and unwilling to spend
core_image: 一句含混的话被手指向它真正要说的那件事，旁边天平恰好停在正中
scene: 统计员把五个读数的总和除开，求出中间的那个数值。The mean of the five readings is nine.
sceneCN: 这里指「一组数的平均值」（第 4 个义项：平均数）；句意为五个读数的平均值是九。可辨识物件：记录纸、五个读数、计算器、天平；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 意思；意义
有意义的
无意义的
刻薄地；吝啬地
刻薄；吝啬

senses.title: To have a sense
senses.definition: to have as a meaning, said of a word, sign or gesture
senses.definitionCN: 指词语、符号或手势所具有的意思
senses.example: What does this symbol mean?
senses.exampleCN: 这个符号表示什么？
senses.why: The Old English verb mænan meant 'to intend, signify', and a word's sense is what it intends.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 mænan 意为「意图、意指」，而词的意思就是它所意图的东西。

senses.title: To be a sign of
senses.definition: to be a sign or indication of something else
senses.definitionCN: 作为另一件事的迹象或征兆
senses.example: A red sky at night means fair weather tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚的红霞意味着明天天气晴好。
senses.why: A sign points to what it intends, so the verb extends from words to natural signs.
senses.whyCN: 符号指向它所意指之物，于是这个动词从词语扩展到自然征兆。

senses.title: To intend to do
senses.definition: to have something in mind as a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把某事放在心里作为目的
senses.example: I mean to finish the report tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我打算今晚把报告写完。
senses.why: Intention is the inward side of meaning: what a person means is what he intends.
senses.whyCN: 意图是「意思」的内面：一个人意指什么，就是他打算什么。

senses.title: The average of a set
senses.definition: the value obtained by adding all the numbers and dividing by how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 把全部数值相加再除以个数所得的值
senses.example: Add the values and divide by five to get the mean.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些值相加再除以五，就得到平均值。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source: Old French meien 'middle', from Latin medianus, not from the English verb.
senses.whyCN: 这一义出自另一来源：古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus，与英语动词无关。

senses.title: The middle between extremes
senses.definition: a middle point equally distant from two extremes
senses.definitionCN: 与两个极端等距的中间点
senses.example: The golden mean lies between excess and defect.
senses.exampleCN: 中庸之道位于过度与不足之间。
senses.why: The same 'middle' sense serves ethics as well as arithmetic, naming the point that is neither too much nor too little.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「中间」义既用于算术也用于伦理，指既不过多也不过少的那一点。

senses.title: Unkind in manner
senses.definition: unkind, spiteful or deliberately hurtful
senses.definitionCN: 不友善、带恶意或故意伤人的
senses.example: It was mean of him to laugh at her mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 他嘲笑她的错误，未免刻薄。
senses.why: The adjective comes from a third source, Old English gemæne 'common, shared', whose sense sank from 'common' to 'inferior' and then to 'petty'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词出自第三个来源，古英语 gemæne「共同的、共享的」，词义从「共同」降到「低劣」，再降到「小气」。

senses.title: Stingy with money
senses.definition: unwilling to spend or share what one has
senses.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或不愿分享所有
senses.example: He is too mean to buy a second chair.
senses.exampleCN: 他太吝啬，连第二把椅子都不肯买。
senses.why: A person who keeps everything for himself is 'common' in the old sense of ordinary and small, and the word settled into stinginess.
senses.whyCN: 把一切都留给自己的人在旧义上显得「普通而小气」，于是这个词固定为吝啬。

senses.title: Remarkable in the phrase 'no mean'
senses.titleCN: 固定说法中意为「不小的」
senses.definition: not small or easy, used in the fixed phrase no mean feat
senses.definitionCN: 不小、不容易，用于固定说法「不小的成就」
senses.example: Finishing the climb in one day was no mean feat.
senses.exampleCN: 一天之内爬完这段路可不是小事。
senses.why: The phrase works by understatement: it denies the small reading of the adjective in order to praise.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法用反语：否定形容词「小」的那一面，从而达到称赞。

intro.en: Mean has three separate sources that happen to share one spelling: the verb 'to intend' from Old English mænan, the noun 'average' from Old French meien and Latin medianus, and the adjective 'petty, stingy' from Old English gemæne 'common'.
intro.cn: mean 有三个恰好同形的来源：表示「意图」的动词出自古英语 mænan；表示「平均值」的名词出自古法语 meien 与拉丁 medianus；表示「小气、刻薄」的形容词出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」。

items.en: Mænan meant 'to intend, signify'. Its deeper Germanic origin is not settled; the usual comparison with German meinen is a family resemblance rather than a proved derivation.
items.cn: mænan 意为「意图、意指」。其更早的日耳曼来源无定论；通常把它与德语 meinen 相比，那只是同族相似，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Gemæne meant 'common, shared'. The sense passed from 'common' to 'ordinary, inferior' and then to 'petty, stingy', a downward slide recorded in Middle English.
items.cn: gemæne 意为「共同的、共享的」。词义从「共同」经「普通、低劣」滑向「小气、吝啬」，这一下移在中古英语中已有记录。

items.en: Meien 'middle' entered English in the fourteenth century as the name of the middle value, and it is the source of the average sense.
items.cn: meien「中间」在十四世纪进入英语，指居中的那个数值，是平均值义的来源。

items.en: Medianus 'of the middle' comes from medius 'middle', the same root that gives median, medium and mediate.
items.cn: medianus「中间的」出自 medius「中间」，同一词根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.en: English spelling merged the three histories into one written form, which is why a single entry must keep verb, average and adjective apart.
items.cn: 英语拼写把这三段历史并成一个书写形式，因此同一个词条必须把动词、平均值与形容词分开。

items.en: Exact first citations for each strand are approximate: the verb is Old English, the average noun is fourteenth-century, and the stingy adjective is later Middle English.
items.cn: 三条线索的确切首见书证都只是约数：动词属古英语，平均值名词属十四世纪，吝啬形容词属中古英语后期。

note.en: Group one holds forms and relatives that are easily mistaken for the same word; group two holds words that share one of the three meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是容易被当成同一个词的形式与亲属词；第二组是分别与三种含义之一相近的词。

entries.definition: The third-person singular of the verb, and separately a plural noun meaning 'resources'; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数，另有一个表示「资源、手段」的复数名词；都不是那个形容词。

entries.definition: The past tense and participle of the verb; the spelling no longer shows the vowel of the base.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式与过去分词；拼写已看不出原形元音。

entries.definition: From the same Latin root as the average sense, but it names the middle item of an ordered set, not the sum divided by the count.
entries.definitionCN: 与平均值义同出拉丁词根，但指按序排列后居中的那一项，而非总和除以个数。

entries.definition: Latin medius as a noun: the middle, or a means between two sides; it has nothing to do with intending.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 medius 的名词形式：中间，或两端之间的媒介；与「意图」无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the sum divided by the count; mean is its technical doublet in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指总和除以个数；在统计中 mean 是它的技术性同义词。

entries.definition: To be a sign of something, close to the 'be a sign' sense of mean.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某事的符号，接近 mean 的「预示」义。

entries.definition: To have a purpose, the plain equivalent of the 'plan' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 怀有目的，是「打算」义的直白对应词。

entries.definition: Unwilling to spend or share, the direct synonym of the adjective in its money sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或分享，是形容词在钱财义上的直接同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Three histories share one spelling: intend, middle, and common-turned-petty.
normal.cn: 三段历史共用一种拼写：意图、中间、由「共同」转来的小气。

normal.en: The verb is irregular in sound but regular in pattern: means, meant, meant, meaning.
normal.cn: 动词读音不规则但形式规律：三单、过去式、过去分词、现在分词依次为 means、meant、meant、meaning。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: mean to do, mean well, the mean value, no mean feat.
normal.cn: 固定说法把义项分开：打算做、出于好意、平均值、不小的成就。

normal.en: The average sense came through French, so it belongs with median and medium rather than with the verb.
normal.cn: 平均值义经法语而来，因此它与 median、medium 同族，而不属于动词那一支。

normal.en: The unkind sense began as 'common', which then meant 'ordinary' and finally 'petty'.
normal.cn: 刻薄义起于「共同的」，再变成「普通的」，最后成了「小气的」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at the one thing a vague sentence was trying to say.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手指出一句含混的话真正想说的那件事。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scales settling exactly level, with equal weights on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平恰好停在水平位置，两边重量相等。

abstract.en: Picture a man counting coins twice before he will spend a single one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把硬币数了两遍才肯花掉一枚。

examples.en: A green light means that the road is clear.
examples.cn: 绿灯表示道路畅通。

examples.en: The mean of the class scores rose after the extra lesson.
examples.cn: 加课之后，全班成绩的平均值上升了。

examples.en: It was mean of them to leave her out of the invitation.
examples.cn: 他们把她排除在邀请之外，实在刻薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 动词那一支表示「意图、意指」；平均值那一支来自法语里的「中间」；形容词那一支从「共同的」滑到「普通」，再滑到「小气」。三支同形，要按上下文分开。

root: 三条互不同源的线索合成一个拼写：动词出自古英语 mænan「意图、意指」，更早来源无定论；平均值义出自古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus、medius；形容词义出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」，词义下滑为「低劣、小气」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses come from three histories: intending and signifying, the middle value, and the small or petty. The entry keeps them apart so that no sentence is read through the wrong history.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项来自三段历史：意图与意指、居中的数值、以及小气刻薄。本词条把它们分开，免得用错历史去读一个句子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand points at what a sentence intends, while a balance beside it rests exactly level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指出一句话所意图的东西，旁边的天平恰好水平。

branches.en: SIGNIFY: a word and a red sky both point to what they intend.
branches.cn: 意指：一个词与一片红霞都指向它们所意图的东西。

branches.en: INTEND: purpose is what a person means to do.
branches.cn: 意图：目的就是一个人打算做的事。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE: the average and the golden mean are one position seen numerically and ethically.
branches.cn: 中间：平均值与中庸是同一点在数字与伦理上的两个看法。

branches.en: COMMON TO PETTY: the adjective slid from shared to ordinary to stingy.
branches.cn: 由共同到小气：形容词从「共享」滑到「普通」再到「吝啬」。

branches.en: UNDERSTATEMENT: denying 'small' is a way of saying 'large'.
branches.cn: 反语：否定「小」，正是说「大」。

intro.en: One spelling serves three families, so the affix view must be split: a Germanic verb, a Germanic adjective, and a Latin root for the middle.
intro.cn: 一种拼写服务于三个词族，因此按语素读时必须拆开：一个日耳曼动词、一个日耳曼形容词，以及一个表示「中间」的拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The verb family is Germanic, with no Latin kin; the average sense belongs to Latin medius, which also gives median, medium and mediate.
latinIntro.cn: 动词一族属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族；平均值义属拉丁 medius，同根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.example: The Old English verb is the source of the 'signify' senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词是「意指」诸义的来源。

items.example: The adjective began as 'shared' and ended as 'stingy'.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「共享」开始，最后落到「吝啬」。

items.example: The Latin root supplies the average and middle senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词根提供平均值与中间诸义。
这个派生形容词给出 median。

items.structure: mean + -ing (noun suffix, result of an action)

items.meaning: in a petty or stingy way
items.example: He spoke meanly of the offer.
items.exampleCN: 他刻薄地评价那个提议。

items.meaning: the quality of being petty or stingy
items.exampleCN: 他们的吝啬让客人吃惊。

definition_zh: 肉；食用肉；（果实或坚果的）可食部分；实质；要旨
definition_en: the flesh of animals eaten as food, the soft edible part inside fruit or nuts, or the central substance of something
core_image: 一块放在砧板上的肉，旁边是敲开的坚果，露出里面饱满的果仁
scene: 冬天的炖锅在灶上咕嘟作响，屋里飘着香料味。She added a little salt to the meat and left it to simmer.
sceneCN: 这里是「供食用的肉」（第 1 个义项：动物肉作为食物）；句意为她往肉里加了一点盐，让它慢慢炖。

由 meat 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无肉的」

senses.title: Animal flesh used as food
senses.definition: the flesh of animals, especially cattle, pigs and sheep, eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 尤指牛、猪、羊等动物供人食用的肉
senses.example: The butcher cut the meat into thin slices.
senses.exampleCN: 屠夫把肉切成薄片。
senses.why: Old English mete meant food of any kind; as other foods took their own names, the general word narrowed onto the flesh sold at a butcher's stall.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mete 泛指任何食物；随着其他食物各自有了名字，这个宽泛的词就收窄到肉铺案板上出售的肉。

senses.title: The edible soft part of fruit or nuts
senses.definition: the soft or fleshy part inside a fruit, nut or shell that can be eaten
senses.definitionCN: 水果、坚果或壳内可供食用的柔软部分
senses.example: Crack the shell and scoop out the meat of the walnut.
senses.exampleCN: 敲开壳，把核桃仁挖出来。
senses.why: The idea of the edible inside of a thing was already present in food, so the word was extended to the part of a nut or fruit worth eating.
senses.whyCN: 「某物内部可食的部分」这一想法本就包含在「食物」里，于是词义被扩展到坚果或水果里值得吃的那一部分。

senses.title: The central substance of an idea or text
senses.definition: the most important part or central content of an argument, book or plan
senses.definitionCN: 论点、书或计划中最重要的部分、核心内容
senses.example: The meat of the report is in its final three pages.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的要旨就在最后三页。
senses.why: If flesh is what fills a body, then the substantial part of a text can be called its meat, with the rest treated as bone or wrapping.
senses.whyCN: 如果肉是填满身体的东西，那么一篇文章的实质部分也可以叫它的 meat，其余部分则被看成骨头或包装。

senses.title: Food of any kind, in older usage
senses.definition: solid food in general, the older sense still visible in a few fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 泛指固体食物，这一较古的词义仍残留在少数固定短语中
senses.example: In older English, meat could mean any food a household stored.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的英语里，meat 可以指一户人家储存的任何食物。
senses.why: This is the original sense; it survives mainly in old texts and in the fixed phrase meat and drink, while everyday usage keeps only the flesh sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的词义；它主要残存在旧文本与固定短语 meat and drink 里，日常用法只保留了「肉」这一义项。

intro.en: Meat began as a general word for food and narrowed to animal flesh, a shift whose exact cause is not settled.
intro.cn: meat 起初是泛指食物的词，后来收窄为动物肉，这一变化的确切原因尚无定论。

items.en: The reconstructed noun *matiz meant food, and its earlier origin is uncertain; no reliable Latin cognate is recorded.
items.cn: 重构名词 *matiz 意为食物，其更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.en: Old English mete meant food or nourishment of any kind, not flesh in particular.
items.cn: 古英语 mete 泛指食物或营养，并不专指肉。

items.en: Middle English kept the broad sense, and meat could still name bread, fruit or drink in the same sentence.
items.cn: 中古英语保留宽泛的词义，meat 仍可与面包、水果或饮料并列。

items.en: Usage narrowed towards animal flesh, though scholars do not agree on a single cause for the change.
items.cn: 词义逐渐收窄到动物肉，不过学者对变化的确切原因并无一致结论。

items.en: The flesh sense dominates, while the older idea survives in compounds and in the figurative sense of substance.
items.cn: 「肉」的义项占主导，较古的词义则保存在复合词与「实质」的比喻义里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the flesh family and one word that merely sounds the same; the near-meaning group collects names for flesh and for kinds of meat.
note.cn: 形近组收「肉」这一族词，外加一个只是读音相同的词；近义组收表示肉与各种肉类的词。

entries.definition: Full of meat, or rich and substantial in content.
entries.definitionCN: 多肉的；内容丰富的。

entries.definition: A ball of minced meat cooked in sauce or soup.
entries.definitionCN: 用肉末做成、在酱汁或汤里煮的丸子。

entries.definition: Made or eaten without meat.
entries.definitionCN: 不含肉或以无肉方式食用的。

entries.definition: To come together with someone; only the sound and spelling are close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人会面；只是读音和拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The soft body tissue of a person or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 人或动物身上的软组织。

entries.definition: Meat from cattle, a specific kind of red meat.
entries.definitionCN: 牛肉，一种具体的红肉。

entries.definition: Meat from pigs.
entries.definitionCN: 猪肉。

entries.definition: Wild animals hunted for food, or their meat.
entries.definitionCN: 供食用的野味或其肉。

normalIntro.en: The word started wide and ended narrow, and the old width still shows in a few compounds and in the sense of substance.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从宽泛起步、以狭窄收场，旧日的宽泛仍体现在少数复合词与「实质」义里。

normal.en: Old English mete was a general word for food, so the ancestor of meat had nothing to do with animals.
normal.cn: 古英语 mete 是泛指食物的词，所以 meat 的祖先与动物无关。

normal.en: The narrowing to flesh happened gradually, and nobody can point to one single cause.
normal.cn: 收窄为「肉」是逐渐发生的，没有人能指出唯一的原因。

normal.en: The adjective meaty adds -y, and meatless adds -less, two small endings that show the flesh sense clearly.
normal.cn: 形容词 meaty 加 -y，meatless 加 -less，两个小后缀清楚显示了「肉」的义项。

normal.en: Meatball is a plain compound: meat plus ball, the shape named directly.
normal.cn: meatball 是直白的复合词：meat 加 ball，直接以形状命名。

normal.en: The meat of a walnut or the meat of an argument keeps the old idea of the edible or substantial inside.
normal.cn: 核桃的 meat 或论点的 meat，都保留了「内部可食或实质部分」的旧想法。

abstract.en: Picture a butcher's block: the word food shrank until it fit exactly on that block.
abstract.cn: 想象一块肉铺的砧板：food 这个词不断缩小，直到正好落在砧板上。

abstract.en: Every language has words that start wide and end narrow, and meat is one of the clearest examples.
abstract.cn: 每种语言都有由宽变窄的词，meat 就是最清楚的例子之一。

abstract.en: Cut a nut open and the same word appears again, this time for the good part inside.
abstract.cn: 把坚果切开，同一个词又出现了，这次指里面最好的那部分。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是身体上可食的部分；义项从动物肉移到坚果内部，最后移到论点的实质。

branches.cn: 屠夫在砧板上切一大块肉

branches.cn: 敲开的核桃露出果仁

branches.en: a reader underlining the last pages

branches.en: an old kitchen storing bread and drink

intro.cn: 这个词条由古英语的食物名词、它的日耳曼语来源、两个能产后缀和两个日常复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for meat; Latin carō, the word for flesh, is a synonym rather than a relative.
latinIntro.cn: meat 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语 carō 表示「肉」，只是近义词而非同源词。

definition_zh: 医疗的；医学的；内科的；身体状况的；（名词）体检
definition_en: relating to the practice, profession or study of medicine, to treatment that is not surgical, or to a person's health and health records
core_image: 白大褂口袋里露出一截听诊器，背后夹着一叠病历
scene: 她车里放着急救箱，包里带着医院的病历。She kept a medical kit in the car and a copy of her hospital records in her bag.
sceneCN: 这里 medical 是「医疗的、医学的」（第 1 个义项：属于医疗职业与医学学科）；句意：她在车里放着医药箱，包里带着一份病历复印件。场景要点：一只白色药箱、一叠写满记录的纸、袋口露出的听诊器；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 医疗的；医学的；内科的；与健康状况有关的
体检（英式口语，medical examination 的缩略）

senses.title: Of the profession
senses.titleCN: 医疗职业与学科：属于医生这一行
senses.definition: relating to the profession, practice or study of medicine
senses.definitionCN: 与医学职业、医疗实践或医学学科有关的
senses.example: She applied to three medical schools and was accepted by two.
senses.exampleCN: 她申请了三所医学院，被其中两所录取。
senses.why: Medical entered English in the 1640s from Late Latin medicalis, 'of a physician', from medicus 'physician'. The adjective first names whatever belongs to doctors.
senses.whyCN: medical 于 17 世纪 40 年代从晚期拉丁语 medicalis 进入英语，意为“医生的”，源自 medicus“医生”。这个形容词最初用来命名一切属于医生的东西。

senses.title: Medical versus surgical
senses.titleCN: 内科的：与外科相对的那一半
senses.definition: relating to treatment by drugs and other non-surgical means, as opposed to surgery
senses.definitionCN: 指以药物及其他非手术手段进行的治疗，与外科相对
senses.example: He was moved from the surgical ward to the medical ward for observation.
senses.exampleCN: 他从外科病房转到内科病房接受观察。
senses.why: Inside one profession, medical marks the branch that treats with medicine rather than the knife. The word draws a line within the hospital, not outside it.
senses.whyCN: 在同一个行业内部，medical 标记的是用药物而不是用刀的那一支。这个词画的是医院内部的界线，而不是对外的界线。

senses.title: The patient's condition
senses.titleCN: 身体状况与病史：属于这个人的健康
senses.definition: relating to a person's health, illnesses and physical condition
senses.definitionCN: 与某人的健康、疾病和身体状况有关的
senses.example: The form asks for your medical history and any allergies.
senses.exampleCN: 这张表格要求填写你的病史和过敏情况。
senses.why: The adjective shifts from the profession to the patient: what belongs to the physician's domain becomes the record of a body's past.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从职业转到病人身上：原本属于医生领域的东西，变成了一个身体过往的记录。

senses.title: A medical: the check-up
senses.titleCN: 体检：形容词被剪成一个名词
senses.definition: a medical examination
senses.definitionCN: 体检；医学检查
senses.example: He passed his medical and joined the crew in March.
senses.exampleCN: 他通过了体检，三月加入了船员队伍。
senses.why: Recorded from 1917 as a shortening of medical examination. English often clips a familiar adjective-plus-noun phrase into the adjective alone.
senses.whyCN: 1917 年起有记录，是 medical examination 的缩略。英语常把熟悉的“形容词加名词”词组剪成只剩形容词。

senses.title: A medical: the doctor
senses.titleCN: 医学生、医生：旧时的口语名词
senses.definition: in older colloquial use, a medical student or a doctor
senses.definitionCN: 旧时口语中指医科学生或医生
senses.example: The old novels speak of a medical coming to the house at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 旧小说里常写一位医生半夜上门。
senses.why: The noun use is recorded from 1823. A person is named by what he or she studies or practises, so the adjective stands alone as a human subject.
senses.whyCN: 名词用法自 1823 年有记录。人被以他所学或所做的事来称呼，于是这个形容词单独站出来指人。

senses.title: Medical evidence
senses.titleCN: 法律与保险中的医学鉴定
senses.definition: used of reports, evidence and certificates that come from doctors and carry legal or official weight
senses.definitionCN: 指来自医生、具有法律或官方效力的报告、证据与证明
senses.example: The court ordered a medical report before deciding on the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 法院在裁定索赔之前下令出具一份医学报告。
senses.why: Once medicine enters law, its documents become evidence. Medical marks the source of authority behind the paper.
senses.whyCN: 一旦医学进入法律，它的文书就成了证据。medical 标记的是这张纸背后的权威来源。

senses.title: Medical equipment
senses.titleCN: 器械与技术：复合词里的限定语
senses.definition: used in compounds for equipment, imaging and technology employed in health care
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词，指医疗照护中使用的设备、影像与技术
senses.example: The charity shipped medical supplies and two portable ultrasound machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构运去了医疗物资和两台便携超声仪。
senses.why: As a classifying adjective it can attach to any object used in care, from a glove to a scanner, without changing its own meaning.
senses.whyCN: 作为分类形容词，它可以附着在任何用于照护的物件上，从手套到扫描仪，而自身含义不变。

senses.title: Medical leave
senses.titleCN: 病假与证明：制度里的一个类别
senses.definition: used in employment contexts for leave or certificates that excuse absence because of illness
senses.definitionCN: 用于雇佣语境，指因病请假或证明缺勤正当的证明文件
senses.example: She took five days of medical leave after the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 手术之后她请了五天病假。
senses.why: Institutions need a word for absence backed by a doctor. Medical turns an illness into a recognised administrative category.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个词来指“有医生作保的缺勤”。medical 把一场病变成一个被承认的行政类别。

senses.title: Medical, not medicinal
senses.titleCN: 与 medicinal 的分界：说用途，不说药效
senses.definition: describing the setting or profession of health care, not the healing power of a substance
senses.definitionCN: 描述医疗的场景或职业，而不是某物质本身具有的治疗效力
senses.example: Medical use is the right phrase for a clinic; medicinal use describes a herb that actually heals.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所的用途该说医疗用途；而药用价值说的是某种草药确实能治病。
senses.why: Medicinal arrived first, in the mid-14th century, meaning 'having curative properties'. Medical came later and names the profession, so the pair divides into 'who treats' and 'what cures'.
senses.whyCN: medicinal 先到，14 世纪中叶就有，意为“具有治疗效力的”。medical 来得更晚，命名的是职业，于是这一对词分成“谁来治”与“什么能治”。

intro.en: Medical is a Latin adjective borrowed through French, built on medicus 'physician'. Its root means 'take appropriate measures', not 'middle', and it has no connection with method. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: medical 是经法语借入的拉丁语形容词，建立在 medicus“医生”之上。它的词根意为“采取恰当措施”，不是“中间”，并且与 method 毫无关系。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'pertaining to the art or profession of healing, or to those who practise it'. It came through French médical from Late Latin medicalis 'of a physician'.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 17 世纪 40 年代，意为“与治疗之术或行业、与行医者有关的”。它经法语 médical 来自晚期拉丁语 medicalis“医生的”。

items.en: Latin medicus was both a noun, 'physician, surgeon, medical man', and an adjective, 'healing, medicinal'. It comes from medeor 'to cure, heal', originally 'know the best course for'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 medicus 既是名词“医生、外科医生、医者”，也是形容词“治疗的、药用的”。它来自 medeor“治愈、治疗”，原义为“知道最好的做法”。

items.en: The root *med- means 'take appropriate measures'. De Vaan explains medeor as a shift from 'measure' to 'distribute a cure, heal'; Avestan vi-mad- 'physician' belongs to the same family.
items.cn: 词根 *med- 意为“采取恰当措施”。de Vaan 把 medeor 解释为从“量度”转向“分配药剂、治疗”；阿维斯陀语 vi-mad-“医生”同属这一族。

items.en: The earlier English adjective in this sense was medicinal, 'having healing or curative properties', from Latin medicinalis. Medical later took over the professional sense.
items.cn: 英语中较早表示这一意义的形容词是 medicinal，即“有治疗或治愈效力的”，来自拉丁语 medicinalis。medical 后来接管了职业性的那一层意义。

items.en: The noun is recorded from 1823 colloquially for 'a medical student or practitioner', and from 1917 as a shortening of medical examination.
items.cn: 名词用法 1823 年起有口语记录，指“医科学生或医生”；1917 年起则是 medical examination（体检）的缩略。

items.en: Medical and method share only their letters. Method is Greek methodos, meta 'in pursuit of' plus hodos 'road'; no Latin medicus is involved. The -met- shape in the two words is a coincidence, and medicine (c. 1200) likewise comes from medicina, not from medical.
items.cn: medical 与 method 只共享字母外形。method 是希腊语 methodos，由 meta“追寻”加 hodos“路”构成，其中没有任何拉丁语 medicus 的成分。两个词里的 -met- 外形纯属巧合；medicine（约 1200 年）同样来自 medicina，而不是来自 medical。

note.en: The first group is the real medic- family: the substance, the healing property, the act of dosing, and the pills themselves. The second group compares adjectives used in and around health care.
note.cn: 第一组是真正的 medic- 词族：医学本身、治疗效力、用药动作、以及药片本身。第二组比较医疗领域内外的几个形容词。

entries.definition: the science and practice of treating disease, or a substance taken to treat illness. It is the thing and the field; medical is only the adjective that points at them.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗疾病的科学与实践，或用来治病的物质。它是事物与领域本身；medical 只是指向它们的形容词。

entries.definition: having curative properties, or used as a medicine. A medicinal herb heals; a medical herb is merely one a doctor might study.
entries.definitionCN: 具有治疗效力的，或作药用的。medicinal 的草药能治病；medical 的草药只是医生可能会研究的那种草。

entries.definition: to treat with medicine, or to add a drug to something. It names the act that medical describes only indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 用药物治疗，或往某物里加药。它命名的是 medical 只间接描述的那个动作。

entries.definition: a medicinal substance, or the treatment of a condition with drugs. Since 1942 it has been the everyday word for prescribed pills.
entries.definitionCN: 药物，或用药物处理某种病情。自 1942 年起，它成了“处方药”的日常说法。

entries.definition: relating to the observation and treatment of patients, or to a clinic. Clinical stresses the setting and the method; medical stresses the profession as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 与病人的观察和治疗有关的，或与诊所相关的。clinical 强调场景与方法；medical 强调整个行业。

entries.definition: relating to the healing of disease, or having a calming or restorative effect. It is closer to medicinal than to medical.
entries.definitionCN: 与疾病治疗有关的，或有镇静、康复效果的。它更接近 medicinal，而不是 medical。

entries.definition: relating to surgery. It is the usual opposite of medical inside a hospital, where medical means treatment by drugs rather than by operation.
entries.definitionCN: 与外科手术有关的。在医院内部它常是 medical 的对立面，那里的 medical 指用药物治疗而非手术。

entries.definition: relating to the auxiliary services that support medical work, such as ambulance crews and lab technicians. The prefix para- 'beside' marks the supporting role.
entries.definitionCN: 与辅助医疗服务有关的，如救护人员与化验员。前缀 para-“在旁边”标记的是支持性的角色。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin medicus 'physician', mederi 'to heal', the older adjective medicinal, and the modern family medicine, medication, medic.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 medicus“医生”、mederi“治疗”、更早的形容词 medicinal，以及现代的 medicine、medication、medic 词族。

normal.en: medic- means 'physician'. Medical is simply the adjective of the doctor's world, as in medical school and medical records.
normal.cn: medic- 表示“医生”。medical 就是医生那个世界的形容词，如 medical school（医学院）、medical records（病历）。

normal.en: The deeper root *med- means 'take appropriate measures'. Healing began as the art of knowing the right measure.
normal.cn: 更深的词根 *med- 意为“采取恰当措施”。治疗最初就是“知道该用多少分量”的技艺。

normal.en: medicinal is older and means 'having healing power'; medical is younger and means 'of the profession'. A medicinal plant heals, a medical student studies.
normal.cn: medicinal 更老，意为“有治疗效力的”；medical 更年轻，意为“属于这一行业的”。药草能治病，医学生则在读书。

normal.en: A medical (noun) is a check-up: the adjective swallowed the noun examination in 1917.
normal.cn: 名词 a medical 就是体检：1917 年这个形容词把名词 examination 吞掉了。

normal.en: Method looks similar but is Greek: meta plus hodos 'road'. Medical has no road in it, only a physician.
normal.cn: method 看着像，其实是希腊语：meta 加 hodos“路”。medical 里面没有路，只有一个医生。

abstract.en: Picture a white coat with two pockets: one holds a stethoscope, the other a folder of records. The coat is medical; the herb in the garden is medicinal.
abstract.cn: 想象一件白大褂有两个口袋：一个装听诊器，一个装一叠病历。这件外套是 medical；园子里的那株草药是 medicinal。

abstract.en: The word always points at people and their apparatus, never at the power of a plant. That is why a hospital is medical and a cough syrup is medicinal.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是指向人及其器械，从不指向植物的效力。所以医院是 medical，止咳糖浆是 medicinal。

abstract.en: A whole institution hides behind three syllables: school, ward, record, certificate, leave. Each is a room the adjective has learned to enter.
abstract.cn: 三个音节背后藏着一整套机构：学院、病房、病历、证明、病假。每一个都是这个形容词学会进入的房间。

examples.en: The village has no medical staff, only a nurse who comes twice a week.
examples.cn: 这个村子没有医务人员，只有一名每周来两次的护士。

examples.en: The insurance company asked for the medical report before paying.
examples.cn: 保险公司在付款前要求提供医学报告。

examples.en: She was on medical leave for a month and came back thinner and quieter.
examples.cn: 她休了一个月病假，回来时瘦了，也沉默了。

dict_mnemonic.text: “麦迪扣”——麦迪把白大褂的扣子扣好，口袋里插着听诊器 → medical 医疗的、医学的（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 medicus“医生”与 mederi“治疗”，词根 *med- 意为“采取恰当措施”，核心是“为身体采取正确的救治手段”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of medical, all radiating from one point: whatever belongs to the physician's world — the school, the ward, the record, the certificate, the machine — and finally the patient's own body as that world describes it.
sensesIntro.cn: medical 的九个义项都从一个点辐射出去：一切属于医生世界的东西——学院、病房、病历、证明、机器——最后是那个世界所描述的病人身体本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white coat whose pockets hold a stethoscope and a folder of records.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件白大褂，口袋里装着听诊器和一叠病历。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: medical names the field and also the drug-treating half of it, set against surgery.
branches.cn: 行业：medical 命名这一领域，也命名其中用药治疗的那一半，与外科相对。

branches.en: THE BODY: the adjective moves from doctors to the patient, naming health, illness and history.
branches.cn: 身体：这个形容词从医生移到病人身上，命名健康、疾病与病史。

branches.en: CLIPPED NOUNS: English shortens 'medical examination' to a medical, and once shortened 'medical man' to the same form.
branches.cn: 截短名词：英语把 medical examination 缩成 a medical，也曾把 medical man 缩成同一个形式。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: law, insurance and employment turn medical into documents, evidence and leave.
branches.cn: 制度：法律、保险与雇佣把 medical 变成文书、证据与病假。

branches.en: OBJECTS AND BOUNDARY: the adjective classifies equipment, and stops short of medicinal, which describes healing power rather than professional setting.
branches.cn: 物件与边界：这个形容词为器械分类，同时止步于 medicinal——后者描述治疗效力，而不是职业场景。

intro.en: Medical is Latin medicus plus the adjective ending -alis, softened in English to -al. The stem medic- is not a free English word, but it carries the whole family.
intro.cn: medical 是拉丁语 medicus 加形容词词尾 -alis，进入英语后软化为 -al。词干 medic- 在英语里不能单独成词，却撑起整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin medicus 'physician' and mederi 'to heal' go back to PIE *med- 'take appropriate measures'. Latin medicina gave English medicine; medicinalis gave medicinal; medicatio gave medication. There is no Greek element in medical.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 medicus“医生”与 mederi“治疗”可追溯到原始印欧语 *med-“采取恰当措施”。拉丁语 medicina 给出英语 medicine；medicinalis 给出 medicinal；medicatio 给出 medication。medical 里没有任何希腊语成分。

items.meaning: of or relating to medicine and physicians
items.meaningCN: 医疗的；医学的（medic- 医生 + -al 形容词词尾）
items.example: The medical team arrived before the ambulances.
items.exampleCN: 医疗队在救护车之前就到了。

items.meaningCN: 医学；医术；药物（-ine 构成名词）
items.example: Medicine has changed more in thirty years than in three centuries.
items.exampleCN: 医学在三十年里的变化超过了过去三个世纪。

items.example: The root has a medicinal taste that children hate.
items.exampleCN: 这种根有孩子讨厌的药味。

items.meaningCN: 用药物治疗；给……用药（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: The water is medicated with chlorine.

items.meaning: treatment with drugs; a medicinal substance
items.meaningCN: 药物治疗；药物（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: He takes his medication after breakfast.

items.meaning: in medical terms; from a medical point of view
items.meaningCN: 从医学上讲（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 这种情况在医学上无法解释。

items.meaning: a doctor, student of medicine, or battlefield medical orderly
items.meaningCN: 医生；医学生；战地卫生员（截短词干）
items.example: A medic stopped the bleeding at the roadside.
items.exampleCN: 一名卫生员在路边止住了血。

items.meaning: relating to biology and medicine together
items.meaningCN: 生物医学的（bio- 生命 + medical）
items.example: The lab won a grant for biomedical research.
items.exampleCN: 该实验室获得了生物医学研究的资助。

items.meaning: supporting medical work without being a doctor
items.meaningCN: 辅助医疗的（para- 在旁边 + medical）
items.example: Paramedical staff handle the first response.
items.exampleCN: 辅助医疗人员负责第一时间的处置。

items.meaning: of the studies taken before medical school
items.meaningCN: 医学预科的（pre- 之前 + medical）
items.example: She finished her premedical courses in two years.
items.exampleCN: 她两年读完了医学预科课程。

items.meaning: a substance used as a remedy
items.meaningCN: 药物；药剂（-ment 构成名词）
items.example: The old pharmacopoeia lists hundreds of medicaments.
items.exampleCN: 那本旧药典列了数百种药剂。

latinEntries.meaning: to cure, heal; originally 'to know the best course for'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 治愈；原义“知道最好的做法”

definition_zh: 药；药物；医学；内科
definition_en: a substance taken to treat or prevent illness, and also the science or practice of healing, including the branch that treats illness without surgery
core_image: 一只棕色玻璃药瓶放在一本翻开的厚医书上，瓶口的软木塞还留着药粉的痕迹
scene: 老式诊所的木架上，一只棕色药瓶和一本翻旧的医书并排放着，瓶身标签已经泛黄。The old doctor said the medicine tasted bitter but worked quickly.
sceneCN: 这里是「药、药物」（第 1 个义项：服用的药）；句意为老医生说这药虽苦却见效快。图中可辨识物件：棕色药瓶、医书、木架。

derivatives.zh: 由 medicine 的词干 medic 加 -al 构成，义为「医学的；医疗的」
由同一词干加 -inal 构成，义为「药用的；有疗效的」
由 medicinal 加 -ly 构成，义为「作为药物地」
由同一词干加 -ment 构成，义为「药物；药剂」

senses.title: A substance taken to treat illness
senses.definition: a substance, especially one taken by mouth, used to treat or prevent illness
senses.definitionCN: 用来治疗或预防疾病的物质，尤指口服的
senses.example: Take this medicine after meals and keep it out of reach of children.
senses.exampleCN: 这药饭后服用，并放在孩子拿不到的地方。
senses.why: Latin medicina first named the healing art, and because the art needed materials, the word came to name the substances themselves.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 medicina 起初指医术，而医术需要材料，于是这个词也用来指那些材料本身。

senses.title: The science and practice of healing
senses.definition: the science and practice of diagnosing, treating and preventing disease
senses.definitionCN: 诊断、治疗与预防疾病的科学与实践
senses.example: She chose medicine because she wanted to understand how the body fails.
senses.exampleCN: 她选择学医，因为她想弄懂身体是怎样出故障的。
senses.why: The same Latin word named the art of healing as a whole, so the discipline kept the older, broader sense.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁词本就指整体的医术，因此这一学科保留了更早、更宽的含义。

senses.title: The branch that avoids surgery
senses.definition: the branch of medicine that treats disease through drugs and diet rather than surgery
senses.definitionCN: 以药物与饮食而非手术来治病的医学分支，与外科相对
senses.example: He was moved from surgery to medicine when the operation was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 手术取消后，他从外科转到内科。
senses.why: When surgery split off as its own craft, the parent word stayed with the non-surgical side, so medicine also names that department.
senses.whyCN: 当外科独立成一门技艺，母词就留在不动刀的一边，于是 medicine 也指那个科室。

senses.title: Something that improves a bad situation
senses.definition: something that improves a difficult situation, used figuratively as if it were a cure
senses.definitionCN: 比喻能改善困境的事物，好像一剂解药
senses.example: Laughter is good medicine for a tired crew.
senses.exampleCN: 笑声对疲惫的船员是一剂良药。
senses.why: Anything that heals can be called medicine, so the word extends easily from pills to comfort, rest or humour.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能治病的东西都能叫 medicine，于是词义很自然地从药片延伸到安慰、休息或幽默。

intro.en: Medicine goes back to a Latin verb for healing, and the same root produced the doctor, the art and the substances, senses English still keeps apart.
intro.cn: medicine 可追溯到拉丁语表示医治的动词，同一词根生出医生、医术与药物，英语至今把这几个义项分开使用。

items.en: Mederi meant to heal, and it supplied the verb behind physician, remedy and medicine alike.
items.cn: mederi 意为医治，是 physician、remedy 与 medicine 共同的动词来源。

items.en: Medicus was the physician, and medicina was the healing art that this person practised.
items.cn: medicus 指医生，medicina 指这位医生所行的医术。

items.en: Medicina covered both the art of healing and the substances used in it, a double sense from the start.
items.cn: medicina 同时指医术与所用之物，从一开始就是双义。

items.en: Old French medecine kept both senses and handed them to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 medecine 保留这两种含义，并在诺曼时期之后传给英语。

items.en: English medicine now leans on drugs in daily speech, while the discipline and the hospital department keep the older sense.
items.cn: 现代英语里 medicine 在日常口语中偏向药物，而学科与医院科室保留较早的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same healing root; the near-meaning group collects drugs, remedies and forms of care.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「医治」词根的词；近义组收药物、疗法与照护方式。

entries.definition: Having healing properties, used of herbs or substances rather than the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 有疗效的，多用于草药或物质，而非学科。

entries.definition: Relating to the science or practice of healing.
entries.definitionCN: 与医治的科学或实践有关。

entries.definition: A formal term for a substance used to heal.
entries.definitionCN: 指治病物质的正式说法。

entries.definition: Drugs prescribed for a condition, or the course of taking them.
entries.definitionCN: 为某种病情开出的药，或服药的疗程。

entries.definition: A substance used to treat illness or, differently, one taken for pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 用于治病的物质；也可指为快感而用的毒品。

entries.definition: A treatment that cures or relieves a complaint.
entries.definitionCN: 能治愈或缓解病痛的疗法。

entries.definition: A treatment that ends a disease, or the state of being healed.
entries.definitionCN: 终结疾病的疗法；也指痊愈的状态。

entries.definition: A small dose of medicine shaped for swallowing.
entries.definitionCN: 便于吞服的小剂型药物。

entries.definition: The care and procedures used against an illness.
entries.definitionCN: 针对疾病采取的照护与处置。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for healing; its family keeps returning to the doctor, the art, the substance and the department.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示医治的拉丁动词上，同族词反复回到医生、医术、药物与科室。

normal.en: Mederi in Latin means to heal, and medicine is the whole effort built on that verb.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mederi 意为医治，medicine 就是建立在这个动词上的整套努力。

normal.en: Medicus is the doctor; medicina is both the art and what the art uses.
normal.cn: medicus 是医生，medicina 既是医术，也是医术所用的东西。

normal.en: Medical adds -al and describes the field, not a bottle of pills.
normal.cn: medical 加 -al，描述的是这个领域，而不是一瓶药。

normal.en: Medicinal adds -inal and means having the power to heal.
normal.cn: medicinal 加 -inal，意为具有治病效力。

normal.en: The department sense survives in hospital signs, where medicine stands opposite surgery.
normal.cn: 科室义保存在医院标牌上，medicine 与 surgery 相对。

abstract.en: One word holds the art, the pill and the ward, because healing needs knowledge, material and a place to happen.
abstract.cn: 一个词装下了医术、药片与病房，因为治病需要知识、材料与发生的场所。

abstract.en: Calling laughter medicine shows that the word measures not the substance but the relief it brings.
abstract.cn: 把笑声称作良药，说明这个词衡量的不是物质，而是它带来的缓解。

abstract.en: A word that can mean both a science and a bottle reminds us that cure is always part knowledge and part matter.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能指科学又能指药瓶，提醒人治愈总是半靠知识、半靠物质。

examples.en: The medicine worked within an hour and the fever broke.
examples.cn: 药一小时内起效，烧退了。

examples.en: He wants to study medicine in a city hospital.
examples.cn: 他想在城市医院学医。

examples.en: Keep the medicine in a cool, dry place.
examples.cn: 把药放在阴凉干燥处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没事的」——吃了药就没事的；记住 medicine 是药。

root: 拉丁语 mederi（医治）→ medicus（医生）→ medicina（医术、药物），经古法语 medecine 进入英语；同族词多与治疗有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is healing; the senses divide into the substance, the discipline, the hospital branch and the figurative comfort.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是医治；义项分为药物、学科、医院科室与比喻性的安慰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brown glass bottle standing on an open medical book, cork still dusted with powder.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只棕色玻璃药瓶放在一本翻开的厚医书上，瓶口的软木塞还留着药粉的痕迹。

branches.en: a spoon of syrup held out to a child
branches.cn: 递到孩子面前的一勺糖浆

branches.en: a laugh that loosens a tense room
branches.cn: 让紧绷的房间松下来的笑声

branches.en: a lecture hall full of diagrams of the body
branches.cn: 挂满人体图的教学厅

branches.en: a hospital corridor sign pointing away from surgery
branches.cn: 医院走廊里指离外科的指示牌

branches.en: a ward round where pills are checked against charts
branches.cn: 按记录核对药片的查房

intro.en: The word is carried by a Latin verb of healing, the doctor noun, the noun for the art, the French form and English endings that build adjectives.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示医治的拉丁动词、指医生的名词、指医术的名词、法语形式，以及构成形容词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 媒介；手段；媒体；中等的；灵媒
definition_en: a channel or means that carries something between two sides; also the middle point of a scale, and a person who claims to speak with spirits
core_image: 一只手把碗端在身前正中，不高不低，左右都不偏
scene: 戏台上，老艺人把一只小碗端在胸前，碗里盛着半碗水，不多不少，正好让台下看清碗底的纹路。The old performer held the bowl at a medium height so that everyone in the yard could see the pattern inside.
sceneCN: 这里 medium 是「中等的、适中的高度」（第 3 个义项：处在两个极端之间）；句意为老艺人把碗端到中等的高度，好让院子里的人都看清碗里的花纹。

derivatives.zh: medium 的复数形式，专指报纸、电视、网络等新闻传播机构
由 medium 与 sized 复合而成，义为「中等大小的」
由 medium 加表示身份状态的后缀 -ship 构成，义为「通灵的本领」

senses.title: A channel that carries something between two sides
senses.definition: something used to carry information, ideas or influence from one person or place to another
senses.definitionCN: 用来把信息、思想或影响从一方传到另一方的东西
senses.example: Speech was the first medium for passing stories down the generations.
senses.exampleCN: 口头讲述是把故事传给后代的第一种媒介。
senses.why: Latin medius means middle, and a medium literally sits in the middle, so the word starts from the gap it bridges rather than from the message it carries.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 medius 意为「中间的」，媒介就字面地待在中间，所以这个词的起点是它所连接的那道缝隙，而不是它运送的内容。

senses.title: Newspapers and broadcasters taken as one body
senses.definition: the press, television, radio and online outlets considered together as the channel that reaches the public
senses.definitionCN: 把报纸、电视、广播和网络平台合起来看，作为面向公众发声的渠道
senses.example: The story stayed out of the media for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事在媒体上压了三个星期没有露面。
senses.why: Once the channel is owned by companies and staffed by editors, the plural media stops naming a means and starts naming an industry with its own habits and power.
senses.whyCN: 当渠道归公司所有、由编辑操持，复数 media 就不再指某种手段，而是指一个有自己的习惯与权力的行业。

senses.title: Halfway between two extremes
senses.definition: of a size, amount or degree that lies between the largest and the smallest
senses.definitionCN: 大小、数量或程度处在一个区间的中间，不在两端
senses.example: Ask for a medium cup if the strong one keeps you awake.
senses.exampleCN: 如果浓的那款让你睡不着，就要一杯中杯。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the plain picture of the Latin root: a mark in the middle of a scale, chosen because neither end suits the purpose.
senses.whyCN: 形容词义保留了拉丁词根最朴素的画面：刻度中间的那一格，因为两端都不合用才选它。

senses.title: A person who claims to hear the dead
senses.definition: someone who says that messages from the dead reach them and that they can pass replies back
senses.definitionCN: 自称能收到死者的讯息、并把回话带回去的人
senses.example: The medium said a visitor from the other side had sat in the empty chair.
senses.exampleCN: 那位灵媒说，有位来自另一边的访客曾坐在那把空椅子上。
senses.why: Here the person again occupies the middle, standing between the living and the dead as a go-between, which is why this sense keeps the plural mediums instead of media.
senses.whyCN: 这里的人又一次占据中间位置，夹在生者与死者之间充当传话者，所以这个义项复数用 mediums 而不是 media。

intro.en: Medium is Latin for middle. English first borrowed it as a noun for a carrier, then let the plural media grow into the press and kept mediums for spirit talkers and middle sizes.
intro.cn: medium 是拉丁语中表示「中间」的词。英语先把它借作名词指承载之物，之后复数 media 长成「媒体」，而 mediums 留给灵媒与中间尺码。

items.en: Medius was the everyday Latin adjective for middle, used of anything placed between two others.
items.cn: medius 是拉丁语里表示「中间的」常用形容词，凡夹在两者之间的事物都用它。

items.en: The neuter form medium named the middle point of a space and also an element that stood between two others.
items.cn: 中性形式 medium 指空间的中点，也指介于另外两者之间的要素。

items.en: The verb mediare meant to be in the middle or to split something in half, and it produced a family of words about standing between parties.
items.cn: 动词 mediare 意为居于中间或把东西分成两半，派生出一族表示「居间」的词。

items.en: English took medium for whatever carries something else, such as air carrying sound or a person carrying a message.
items.cn: 英语借 medium 指承载他物的东西，例如传声的空气，或替人带话的信使。

items.en: The plural media came to mean the news industry, while mediums stayed with people who contact spirits; both plurals also name sizes that fall between small and large.
items.cn: 复数 media 逐渐指新闻业，mediums 则留给与亡灵沟通的人；两种复数也都用来指介于大小之间的尺码。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root for middle through several English words; the near-meaning group gathers words for a means of passing something on.
note.cn: 形近组沿着表示「中间」的拉丁词根串起几个英语词；近义组收表示「传递某物的手段」的词。

entries.definition: To stand between two sides and help them settle a dispute.
entries.definitionCN: 站在两方之间，帮他们解决争端。

entries.definition: Belonging to the Middle Ages, the period between ancient and modern times.
entries.definitionCN: 属于中世纪的，即古代与近代之间的时期。

entries.definition: Happening at once, with nothing standing in between.
entries.definitionCN: 立刻发生的，中间没有间隔。

entries.definition: Only middling in quality, neither good nor bad.
entries.definitionCN: 质量平平的，既不好也不坏。

entries.definition: A method or thing used to get a result.
entries.definitionCN: 用来达到结果的方法或东西。

entries.definition: A route or system through which something is passed on.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物传出去的途径或系统。

entries.definition: Something that carries an idea or a message, as well as a machine that carries people.
entries.definitionCN: 既指载人的交通工具，也指承载思想或讯息的东西。

entries.definition: The power or means by which something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 做成某事所凭借的力量或手段。

normalIntro.en: The whole family circles one Latin idea, the middle, and the word keeps that position in every sense it takes on.
normalIntro.cn: 整族词都绕着拉丁语的一个意思——「中间」——打转，这个词每多一个义项，也仍然站在那个位置上。

normal.en: Medius is Latin for middle, so a medium is literally what sits in the middle between two sides.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 medius 意为中间，所以 medium 字面上就是夹在两方中间的那个东西。

normal.en: Media is the plural used for news outlets, which is why the word often appears with a plural verb in that sense.
normal.cn: media 是用于新闻机构的复数形式，所以这个义项常与复数动词连用。

normal.en: A medium shirt sits on the middle hook, between the small and the large, and the adjective follows the same picture.
normal.cn: 中号衬衫挂在中间那只钩子上，夹在小号与大号之间，形容词义用的是同一幅画面。

normal.en: Mediums, not media, is the plural for spirit talkers, because those people stand between two worlds rather than between two sizes.
normal.cn: 灵媒的复数是 mediums 而不是 media，因为这些人站在两个世界之间，而不是两个尺码之间。

normal.en: Mediocre comes from the same middle root and means only middling, a useful reminder that middle can also mean unremarkable.
normal.cn: mediocre 出自同一表示「中间」的词根，意为平平无奇，正好提醒人：中间也可以指不出众。

abstract.en: Every medium is a bridge, and a bridge is only noticed when it fails to carry anything across.
abstract.cn: 每个媒介都是一座桥，而桥只有在运不过东西时才会被人注意到。

abstract.en: A word for the middle ends up naming the press, the spirits and the middle shelf, because all three are places where two sides meet.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「中间」的词最后指媒体、亡灵与中间货架，因为这三者都是两方相遇的地方。

abstract.en: To choose a medium is to accept that the shape of the channel quietly shapes what travels through it.
abstract.cn: 选择一种媒介，就等于承认渠道的形状会悄悄塑造从中经过的东西。

examples.en: Air is the medium that carries a voice across a room.
examples.cn: 空气是把声音送过房间的媒介。

examples.en: The news media covered the election through the night.
examples.cn: 新闻媒体整夜报道这场选举。

examples.en: This jacket comes in small, medium and large.
examples.cn: 这件外套有小号、中号和大号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米迪姆」——把米分成两半，正好落在中间；记住 medium 是中间、媒介。

root: 拉丁语 medius（中间的）→ 中性名词 medium（中点、居间之物）；复数 media 后专指媒体，mediums 则保留灵媒义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the middle position. From it grow the carrier between two sides, the press that owns the carriers, the middle of a scale, and the person who stands between the living and the dead.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「中间的位置」。由此长出两方之间的承载物、拥有这些渠道的媒体、刻度上的中间一格，以及站在生者与死者之间的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl held at the exact middle of the body, level with the chest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只碗端在身体正中，与胸口齐平。

branches.en: a messenger handing a letter across a river
branches.cn: 信使在河边把信递到对岸

branches.en: an editor deciding which faces appear on the front page
branches.cn: 编辑决定谁的脸能上头版

branches.en: a shirt hanging on the middle hook of a rack
branches.cn: 衣架中间那只钩子上的一件衬衫

branches.en: a dim room where an unfamiliar voice answers
branches.cn: 昏暗房间里有个陌生的声音回应

branches.en: a scale whose middle mark is the safest choice
branches.cn: 刻度尺上中间那一格最稳妥

intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示「中间」的拉丁词根、它的中性名词、它的动词，以及后来分任两职的两个英语复数形式撑起。

senses.title: To come together with someone by chance or by plan
senses.definition: To come together with someone by chance or by plan
senses.definitionCN: 与某人相遇
senses.example: I met my teacher on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 我在回家路上遇到了老师。
senses.why: Old English metan meant to come upon; a chance meeting and an arranged one share the same picture of two paths crossing.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 metan 意为碰见；偶遇与约见都共享两条路交叉的同一画面。

senses.title: To satisfy a need or a standard
senses.definition: To satisfy a need or a standard
senses.definitionCN: 达到要求或满足需要
senses.example: The school meets the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校符合安全规定。
senses.why: A meeting of two things can also mean a demand and a supply arriving together, so meet took the sense of satisfying.
senses.whyCN: 两样东西相遇也可指需求与供给恰好碰头，于是 meet 有了满足之义。

senses.title: A gathering for sports competitions
senses.definition: A gathering for sports competitions
senses.definitionCN: 体育比赛的集会
senses.example: Our school held a sports meet in May.
senses.exampleCN: 我们学校五月举办了运动会。
senses.why: In British English a meet is a gathering for sport, a short name for the meeting of competitors.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语中 meet 指运动集会，是参赛者相聚的简称。

definition_en: one of the parts or people that make up a group or a body
core_image: 一张长桌四周坐满人，每把椅子背后贴着写了名字的纸牌
scene: 点名时秘书念出一个名字，长桌尽头有人举手，墙上的名册随即在那一行后面打了一个勾。As the secretary read the roll, a hand went up at the far end of the table, and the list on the wall received a tick beside that member.
sceneCN: 这里 member 指「团体中的一名成员」（第 1 个义项）；句意为点名时长桌尽头有人举手应到，墙上的名册在该成员那一行打勾。可辨识物件：长桌、名册、铅笔、举起的手；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: One among many
senses.definition: a person who belongs to a group, team or organization
senses.definitionCN: 属于某团体、队伍或组织的一个人
senses.example: Every member of the team signed the card.
senses.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。
senses.why: The Latin word for a limb was applied to people as parts of a community, and this is the sense that dominates today.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语指「肢体」的词被用来指共同体中的个人，这成了今天最主要的义项。

senses.title: A state among states
senses.definition: a country or organization that belongs to a larger union
senses.definitionCN: 属于更大联盟的国家或组织
senses.example: The member states met to revise the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 各成员国开会修订这项条约。
senses.why: Once a body can be a part of a larger body, whole states take the name that once belonged to persons.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个机构可以是更大机构的一部分，整个国家也就用上了原属个人的称呼。

senses.title: A limb of the body
senses.definition: an arm, leg or other part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 手臂、腿或身体的其他部位
senses.example: The old anatomy text speaks of the body and its members.
senses.exampleCN: 那本古老的解剖学著作谈到身体及其四肢。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the Latin noun named a limb before it named a person in a group.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：这个拉丁名词先指肢体，后指团体中的人。

senses.title: A seat in the house
senses.definition: a person elected or appointed to a legislative assembly
senses.definitionCN: 经选举或任命进入立法机构的个人
senses.example: The member for the northern district spoke last.
senses.exampleCN: 北部选区的议员最后发言。
senses.why: Legislatures borrow the plain word for a group member and make it a title with a constituency attached.
senses.whyCN: 立法机构借用这个表示团体成员的普通词，并给它加上选区，使之成为头衔。

senses.title: An element of a set
senses.definition: an object that belongs to a mathematical set
senses.definitionCN: 属于某一数学集合的对象
senses.example: Each member of the set shares one property.
senses.exampleCN: 集合中的每个元素都共有一种性质。
senses.why: Mathematics needed a neutral word for what is inside a set, and the everyday noun was precise enough.
senses.whyCN: 数学需要一个中性词来指集合内部的东西，而这个日常名词已经足够精确。

senses.title: A part of a frame
senses.definition: one of the beams or parts that make up a structure
senses.definitionCN: 构成某一结构的梁或其他部件
senses.example: Every member of the truss carries part of the load.
senses.exampleCN: 桁架的每个构件都承担一部分荷载。
senses.why: Engineering returns to the limb sense: a frame is a body, and its beams are its members.
senses.whyCN: 工程学回到了「肢体」义：框架是一个躯体，梁就是它的肢体。

senses.title: One of the household
senses.definition: a person belonging to a family or household
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个家庭或住户的人
senses.example: The household has four members, two of them children.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家庭有四名成员，其中两名是孩子。
senses.why: The smallest group a person belongs to is a household, and the word scales down without changing.
senses.whyCN: 一个人所属的最小团体就是家庭，这个词缩小尺度而含义不变。

senses.title: One of a species group
senses.definition: an organism belonging to a particular group in taxonomy
senses.definitionCN: 在分类学上属于某一类群的生物
senses.example: This species is a member of the rose family.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种是蔷薇科的一员。
senses.why: Natural history treats a family as a body and its species as members, completing the same metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 博物学把一个科当作躯体、把其中的物种当作成员，完成了同一个比喻。

intro.en: Member comes from Latin membrum 'limb, part of the body', which Latin also used for a person as a part of a community. English borrowed it through Old French. Its deeper origin is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: member 来自拉丁 membrum「肢体、身体的一部分」，拉丁语也用这个词指作为共同体之部分的个人。英语经古法语借入。其更深来源尚无定论。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Membrum is well recorded for a limb. The extension to a person who is a part of a group is also Latin, not a later English invention.
items.cn: membrum 指肢体有充分书证。把它扩展到「团体之部分的个人」也发生在拉丁语中，并非英语后来的创造。

items.en: The deeper origin of membrum is generally thought to involve a root for cutting or dividing, but the form is a reconstruction and different handbooks word it differently.
items.cn: membrum 的更深来源一般被认为与表示「切割、划分」的词根有关，但该形式属重构，各家手册的表述也不一致。

items.en: Old French membre carried both the limb sense and the social sense, and English took the word in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 membre 同时带有「肢体」义与社会义，英语在十三世纪借入这个词。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word spread to legislatures, mathematics and engineering, each borrowing the part-of-a-whole image.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词扩展到立法机构、数学与工程学，每一处都借用了「整体之一部分」的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Latin form is a reconstruction, so the family image at the base is inferred rather than demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：前拉丁语的形式属重构，因此词底的家庭意象属推断而非实证。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms and one look-alike built on an unrelated root; group two holds words for people who belong to something.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形式，另加一个建在无关词根上的形近词；第二组是表示「属于某处的人」的词。

entries.definition: The status of being a member; member is the person, membership is what that person holds.
entries.definitionCN: 成员的身份；member 是人，membership 是此人所拥有的身份。

entries.definition: To cut a body into parts, built directly on the limb sense of the Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 把身体切成数块，直接建在这个拉丁名词的「肢体」义上。

entries.definition: From re- plus memor 'mindful', not from membrum: it means to recall, and only the sound connects it.
entries.definitionCN: 由 re- 加 memor「留心的」构成，并非来自 membrum：意为回想，只有读音把它联系起来。

entries.definition: Also from memor 'mindful'; the shared letters suggest a limb root that is not there.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自 memor「留心的」；相同的字母让人以为有「肢体」词根，其实并没有。

entries.definition: An organization attached to a larger one; a member can be a person or a body, while an affiliate is always an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 附属于更大机构的组织；member 可以是人也可以是机构，而 affiliate 总是机构。

entries.definition: A colleague or linked firm without formal membership; a member holds a defined place on a roll.
entries.definitionCN: 无正式成员身份的同事或关联公司；member 在名册上拥有明确的位置。

entries.definition: A companion or peer, often in a learned society; fellow stresses equality, member stresses inclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 同伴或同侪，常用于学会；fellow 强调平等，member 强调被纳入。

entries.definition: A person who takes part in an event; a participant need not be on any roll, while a member is.
entries.definitionCN: 参与某项活动的人；参与者不必在名册上，而成员则在名册上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin limb word, the real institutional compounds, and the real derived forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「肢体」词、真实的机构复合词，以及真实的派生形式。

normal.en: A member is a limb of the body of the group: the metaphor is the same at both scales.
normal.cn: 成员是团体的「肢体」：这个比喻在两个尺度上完全一致。

normal.en: The oldest sense is anatomical, which is why dismember means cutting off limbs, not expelling people.
normal.cn: 最古老的义项是解剖学上的，因此 dismember 指切去肢体，而不是开除成员。

normal.en: Compound phrases: member state, family member, staff member, founding member.
normal.cn: 复合搭配：成员国、家庭成员、工作人员、创始成员。

normal.en: A member of parliament is a member first and a representative second, which is why the title keeps the plain word.
normal.cn: 议会议员先是「成员」，其次才是代表，因此这个头衔保留了那个朴素的词。

normal.en: The plural is regular, and the possessive adds an apostrophe with the possessive ending.
normal.cn: 复数按常规变化，所有格则在词尾加撇号与属格标记。

abstract.en: Picture a long table where every chair has a name card taped to its back.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，每把椅子背后都贴着一张写有名字的卡片。

abstract.en: Picture a truss bridge seen as a skeleton, each beam a limb holding the whole up.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桁架桥被看成一具骨架，每根梁都是撑起整体的一肢。

abstract.en: Picture a family photograph in which each face occupies one place in the frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一张全家福，每张脸都在画面里占一个位置。

examples.en: She became a member of the research group in her second year.
examples.cn: 她在第二年成为研究小组的成员。

examples.en: The member states disagreed over the wording of the clause.
examples.cn: 各成员国对条款的措辞意见不一。

examples.en: The fall injured a member of his left hand.
examples.cn: 那次跌倒伤到了他左手的一处肢体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「member = mem（记忆）+ ber」——被记住、被写进名册的人 → 成员、会员

root: 拉丁 membrum「肢体、身体的一部分」；由「躯体之一肢」引申为「团体之一员」。更深词根属重构，不作定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one limb: a person on the roll, a state inside a union, the anatomical limb itself, a seat in a legislature, an element in a set, a beam in a frame, a face in a household, and a species inside a family.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕「一肢」展开：名册上的人、联盟中的国家、解剖意义上的肢体、立法机构中的一席、集合中的元素、框架中的一根梁、家庭中的一张面孔，以及一个科之内的一个物种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table where every chair carries a name card on its back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，每把椅子背后都贴着写有名字的卡片。

branches.en: PERSONS AND HOUSEHOLDS: the person on the roll, and the smallest group that person belongs to.
branches.cn: 个人与家庭：名册上的人，以及此人所归属的最小团体。

branches.en: STATES AND UNIONS: a whole country holding a place inside a larger body.
branches.cn: 国家与联盟：整个国家在更大机构中占据一席。

branches.en: THE OLDEST LAYER: the limb itself, the literal body part behind the metaphor.
branches.cn: 最古老的一层：肢体本身，也就是比喻背后那个字面的身体部位。

branches.en: THE SEAT IN THE HOUSE: a legislator whose title keeps the plain word for a group member.
branches.cn: 议会中的一席：立法者的头衔保留了「团体成员」这个朴素说法。

branches.en: PARTS OF STRUCTURED WHOLE: a set element, a structural beam, and a species inside a family.
branches.cn: 结构整体的各个部分：集合元素、结构构件，以及一个科之内的物种。

intro.en: Member is the Latin limb word reshaped in English, and its family runs from anatomy to institutions.
intro.cn: member 是拉丁语「肢体」一词在英语中的变形，其词族从解剖学一直延伸到制度。

latinIntro.en: Latin membrum yields member and dismember; -ship and non- build the social forms. The Latin noun is third-declension in -um, not a verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 membrum 衍生出 member 与 dismember；-ship 与 non- 构成社会义的形式。这个拉丁名词属 -um 第二变格法，并非动词。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是词族的基础。

items.example: Every member of the team signed the card.
items.exampleCN: 队里的每一名成员都签了卡片。

items.example: The members voted on the proposal.
items.exampleCN: 成员们对这项提案进行了表决。

items.example: Membership carries the right to vote.
Nonmembers may visit on weekdays only.
items.exampleCN: 非会员只能在工作日参观。

items.example: The old chronicle describes how they dismembered the statue.
items.exampleCN: 那部旧编年史描述了人们如何把雕像肢解。

items.meaning: the act or result of cutting apart
items.example: The treaty led to the dismemberment of the kingdom.
items.exampleCN: 这项条约导致王国被分裂。

items.example: The member state blocked the proposal.
items.exampleCN: 该成员国否决了这项提案。

definition_zh: 记忆；记住并回想信息的能力，也可指一段回忆、纪念或计算机存储
definition_en: the ability to remember information and experiences, a remembered event, or the part of a computer that stores data
core_image: 一间库房按编号存放过往片段，取件时按编号调出
scene: 老人闻到医院走廊的消毒水味，立刻想起多年前陪护家人的那个下午。The smell of disinfectant in the corridor brings back the afternoon years ago when she sat beside a sick relative, a sudden act of memory.
sceneCN: 这里 memory 指「唤起过往经历的能力」（第 1 个义项：把过去的片段重新调出）；句意为消毒水的气味让她立刻回到多年前陪护家人的那个下午。图中可辨识物件：医院走廊、消毒水瓶、长椅、被唤起的时间线；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 记忆；记忆力；回忆；纪念；计算机内存

derivatives.zh: 记住；背下来
记忆；背诵
纪念碑；纪念的
难忘的
